It fields five male football teams from Under 12s to open age in the Tallangatta & District Football League, eight netball teams from Under 11s to open age in the Tallangatta & District Netball Association, and four female football teams in the AFL North East Border competition. The club is a not for profit set up to give the community sporting, social and recreation opportunities, with a strong focus on junior development.
highlights: Home ground Thurgoona Oval, 268 Table Top Road
Five football teams from Under 12s to open age
Eight netball teams from Under 11s to open age
Not for profit with a strong junior development focus

name: Jindera Football Netball Club
description: Jindera Football Netball Club was established in 1899 and competes in the Hume Football Netball League. The club describes itself as community built, covering everything from Auskick to seniors, and fields seniors, seconds, Under 17 and Under 14 football sides alongside female football and netball teams. Memberships and club merchandise are sold through its website.
highlights: Competes in the Hume Football Netball League

name: Albury Tigers
description: The Albury Tigers are Albury's football and netball club, established in 1876 and playing in the Ovens & Murray league. The club has grounds and rooms on Wodonga Place in central Albury which include a bar and function rooms. Memberships and club merchandise are sold through the club's online shop.
highlights: Plays in the Ovens & Murray Football Netball League
Grounds and rooms on Wodonga Place in central Albury
Bar and function rooms on site

name: Wodonga Cricket Club
description: Wodonga Cricket Club was founded in 1869 and plays at Martin Park on Gordon Street, where it has two turf wicket ovals, Les Cheesley Oval and John Flower Oval, with electronic scoreboards, practice nets and clubrooms with a bar and kitchen. The club fields junior teams at Under 12, Under 14 and Under 16, senior sides in A Provincial, B Provincial and C Grade, and a women's team in the Cricket Albury Wodonga Thunder Stars league. It also runs an All Abilities program for ages 15 and over and Woolworths Cricket Blast for children from age 4.
highlights: Two turf wicket ovals with electronic scoreboards
Junior teams from Under 12 to Under 16
Women's team in the Thunder Stars league
All Abilities cricket for ages 15 and over

name: Bungam Community Garden
description: Bungam Community Garden started in July 2015 on the corner of Engelhardt and Stanley Streets in Albury, where local residents from the surrounding neighbourhood adopt garden beds and grow produce in a shared space. It takes its name from its position near Bungambrawatha Creek, the area's largest waterway, and is easy to reach from the Bungambrawatha Creek Trail. Visitors are welcome to look around but are asked not to help themselves to produce grown by the volunteer gardeners.
addressLine: Corner Engelhardt Street and Stanley Street
highlights: Corner of Engelhardt and Stanley Streets, Albury
Reached from the Bungambrawatha Creek Trail

name: Yackandandah Community Centre
description: The Yackandandah Community Centre is the town's neighbourhood house at 29 High Street, described as a space for the community to come together, learn from a range of courses, take part in activities and interest groups or browse the op shop. It runs the Yack Chat Cafe, a community garden and an op shop operated as a community social enterprise, and hires out rooms at $20 an hour along with equipment. The centre also runs a grants program for local initiatives and maintains a community directory.
highlights: Neighbourhood house at 29 High Street, Yackandandah
Op shop run as a community social enterprise
Room hire at $20 an hour, plus equipment hire
YCC Grants program for local initiatives

name: Albury Horticultural Society
description: The Albury Horticultural Society has been operating for over 100 years and is a group of avid garden and plant lovers who may or may not have any formal qualifications. It meets on the first Thursday of the month at 7.30pm at the Albury Showground. The society is open to anyone interested in gardening and a little social outing.
highlights: Meets the first Thursday of the month at 7.30pm
Meetings held at the Albury Showground
Open to gardeners of any experience level

name: Albury Chess Club
description: The Albury Chess Club was established in 1977 and plays every Friday night from 8pm until all games finish, at Albury High School in Kiewa Street. The club welcomes players of all standards, from novices and beginners through to the strongest players. It also runs competitions that bring schools and junior players together for titles and trophies.
highlights: Meets at Albury High School, Kiewa Street
Open to players of all standards
Postal address PO Box 488, Lavington NSW 2641

name: Albury Wodonga parkrun
description: Albury Wodonga parkrun is a free, fun and friendly weekly 5km community event held every Saturday at 8am, starting from the Kremur Street Boat Ramp in West Albury. Participants can walk, jog, run, volunteer or spectate. The event is run entirely by volunteers, with weekly rosters and volunteer callouts posted through its Facebook page.
highlights: Starts at the Kremur Street Boat Ramp, West Albury
Walk, jog, run, volunteer or spectate
Volunteer run, with rosters posted on Facebook

name: Hive Rotary Club Australia
description: Hive Rotary Club is a project driven Rotary club that meets fortnightly by Zoom and gathers in person in the Albury-Wodonga area every six weeks. Its projects include Paying It Forward, which takes students to community service projects, Hive & Honey, a social enterprise addressing period poverty through menstrual health and employment, and an environmental education project on Nusa Penida. The club also runs monthly fundraising barbecues and seasonal gift wrapping at Myer Centrepoint.
highlights: Project driven Rotary club based in Albury-Wodonga
Fortnightly Zoom meetings with in person gatherings every six weeks
Paying It Forward youth service program
Hive & Honey social enterprise addressing period poverty

name: The Proprietor
description: A cafe set in a heritage building on Townsend Street whose original foundations were laid before 1890, first a saddler's shop and later a butchery. The kitchen works to a seasonal, locally sourced menu of brunch dishes, pastries, bowls and lunch plates alongside espresso coffee. The owners restored the space using recycled materials and handcrafted furnishings, and there is alfresco seating out the front.
highlights: Housed in a pre-1890 saddlery and former butcher shop
Seasonal menu built on local Albury producers
Brunch, pastries and gourmet lunch plates
Open seven days from 7am weekdays, 8am weekends

name: Mr Benedict
description: A breakfast, brunch and lunch cafe at the Monument end of Dean Street, opposite the Botanic Gardens. The all-day menu runs to eggs benedict, corn fritters, toasties, waffles, salads and burgers, with vegan options through the menu. Coffee is Code Black house blend, and there is a courtyard out the back planted with bamboo.
highlights: Open Wednesday to Sunday, kitchen closes 2pm

name: Coffee Mamma
description: An espresso bar on Dean Street serving freshly roasted coffee with snacks and light food options. They pour exclusive locally roasted blends and single origins, and sell packaged beans for home or office brewing. Trade is early: doors open at 6am on weekdays and close at 2pm.
highlights: Espresso bar on Dean Street in central Albury
Locally roasted exclusive blends and single origins
Retail beans for home and office

name: The River Deck Cafe
description: A cafe and restaurant in Noreuil Park on the bank of the Murray River. The kitchen cooks modern Australian food built on natural, native and local ingredients sourced from regional farmers and producers around Albury-Wodonga. Breakfast and lunch are served seven days from 9am to 3pm, and there is a kids' menu.
highlights: Riverside location in Noreuil Park on the Murray
Modern Australian menu using native and local ingredients
Produce sourced from Albury-Wodonga regional growers
Breakfast and lunch seven days, 9am to 3pm

name: Cafe Musette
description: A Young Street cafe open for breakfast and lunch six days a week, from 7am to 2pm. The kitchen closes at 1.30pm Monday to Friday and 2pm on Saturday. Catering is offered alongside the dine-in and takeaway trade.
highlights: Breakfast and lunch trade six days a week

name: Clancy's Food Store
description: A weekday food store and coffee stop on Smollett Street, trading from 6.15am Tuesday to Friday and 6.45am on Monday. Alongside coffee and treats they run a lunch menu and prepare takeaway gourmet meals fresh each day. Catering is offered for events and business functions.
highlights: Lunch menu plus coffee and treats
Takeaway gourmet meals prepared fresh daily

name: Green Zebra Café
description: A Dean Street cafe open seven days from 7.30am to 3pm. The breakfast menu covers eggs benedict, smashed avocado, pancakes and French toast, and the kitchen also makes preservative-free pasta in house served with Italian sauces. Coffee is made to order.
highlights: Breakfast menu of benedicts, smashed avocado and pancakes
Fresh preservative-free pasta made in house

name: Retro Lane Café
description: A cafe in QEII Square run by AlburyCity as a social enterprise supporting young people aged 12 to 24. The counter serves hot finger food, gourmet sandwiches, house-made baked goods and fresh seasonal fruit at affordable prices. Catering is available for meetings and events.
highlights: Social enterprise run by AlburyCity for young people aged 12-24
Gourmet sandwiches, hot finger food and house-made baked goods

name: Brothers Cup
description: A small batch coffee roaster on Union Road in North Albury. Green coffee is sourced from growers around the world and roasted in-house in small batches so each cup stays fresh and true to origin. They sell retail beans alongside a cafe counter, trading weekday mornings from 6.30am.
highlights: Roasts in small batches on site in North Albury
Retail beans plus a cafe counter

name: Platform 9 Coffee Roasters
description: A family-owned specialty coffee roaster, wholesaler and store on Townsend Street in South Albury. They roast in small batches and supply cafes across the region, with a retail shop for beans and brew gear. The business also runs barista training and provides cafe support and brew recipes.
highlights: Family-owned specialty roaster in South Albury
Small batch roasting with retail store
Wholesale supply and full cafe support

name: Crust & Crumb Bakery
description: A sourdough bakery on the corner of Ebden and Olive Streets in South Albury, opened in 2024 by baker Adam Streltschenko. Loaves are naturally leavened and slow fermented using certified sustainable Australian flour, filtered water and sea salt, in styles including wholewheat and honey, ciabatta, rye, white and pumpkin. The counter also carries almond and plain croissants, Danish pastries, choc chip sourdough biscuits and muffins.

name: Valentine's Bakehouse
description: An artisan sourdough bakery and coffee shop in Myer Centrepoint on David Street. They bake bread daily and serve fresh lunches, hearty sandwiches and homemade cakes using locally sourced ingredients. Coffee is locally roasted White Owl. The business also trades in Wodonga and Rutherglen.
highlights: Sandwiches, fresh lunches and homemade cakes
Pours locally roasted White Owl coffee
Also trades in Wodonga and Rutherglen

name: Beechworth Bakery Albury
description: The Albury shop of the Beechworth Bakery group, trading in Myer Centrepoint since 2004. The counter carries the bakery's Ned Kelly pie, the Beesting and a range of cakes, pastries, pies, breads and rolls, with barista-made coffee. The cafe area has been renovated and catering is available for events.
highlights: Ned Kelly pie and the Beesting
Cakes, pastries, pies, breads and rolls

name: Red Brik Caffe
description: A Sanders Road cafe in Lavington open every day from 8am to 2pm. They cook with quality, locally sourced ingredients and serve all-day breakfast, lunch, cakes and specialty coffee. Gluten free, vegan, vegetarian and dairy free options are on the menu, and takeaway is available.
highlights: All-day breakfast plus lunch and cakes
Gluten free, vegan, vegetarian and dairy free options

name: Close Collective Cafe
description: A High Street cafe in Wodonga, opposite the water tower, serving a fresh and seasonal selection of breakfast, morning tea and lunch. The kitchen describes its food as classic cafe fare made to a consistent high standard, with both savoury and sweet options. Baristas pour locally roasted beans from The Blessed Bean, and a separate brunch menu runs on Saturdays.
highlights: Locally roasted The Blessed Bean coffee
Seasonal breakfast, morning tea and lunch menu

name: BeanStation Cafe
description: An upcycled industrial cafe and wine bar in Wodonga's 1873 railway station building at Junction Place. Old floor beams, tin signs and metal braces have been repurposed through the fit-out, and there is seating out on the platform. The modern Australian menu is served with Merlo coffee, local wines and Australian boutique beers, plus seasonal grazing platters.
addressLine: Tenancy 1, Wodonga Railway Station, Elgin Boulevard
highlights: Set in the 1873 Wodonga railway station at Junction Place
Modern Australian menu and grazing platters
Merlo coffee, local wines and boutique beers
Seating on the old station platform

name: Delibean
description: A Beechworth Road cafe in Wodonga open Monday to Saturday from 7.30am to 4pm. They serve coffee alongside generous all-day breakfasts and cafe lunch favourites, with daily changing specials written up on the blackboards.
highlights: All-day breakfast and cafe lunch menu
Daily changing specials on the blackboards

name: Henri's Wodonga Bakery
description: A Hovell Street bakery in Wodonga making handmade pies, fresh sandwiches and sweet treats, with ingredients bought from local butchers and grocers. The counter covers breakfast and lunch, and they also sell frozen meals and fresh takeaway items. Catering is available. Doors open at 6am on weekdays.
highlights: Ingredients from local butchers and grocers
Handmade pies, fresh sandwiches and sweet treats
Breakfast and lunch to dine in or take away
Homemade frozen meals and a catering menu

name: Gum Tree Pies Wodonga
description: The Wodonga shop of Gum Tree Pies, a pie maker whose pies are made in Yackandandah. The Aurora Way store trades 8am to 4pm seven days and also takes orders online. The business runs shops in Yackandandah, Wodonga and Bright.
highlights: One of three Gum Tree Pies stores

name: Piccolo Pod
description: A coffee window on Elgin Boulevard in Wodonga operating out of a converted shipping container. The team serve coffee and milkshakes, with plenty of outdoor seating on the lawns around the pod.
highlights: Coffee served from a converted shipping container
On Elgin Boulevard near Junction Place

name: Beechworth Bakery
description: The original Beechworth Bakery on Camp Street, established in 1984 when Tom O'Toole bought the Ideal Cafe and turned it into a bakery. It is the birthplace of the Ned Kelly pie, a meat pie topped with bacon, cheese and a whole egg, and of the Beesting. The counter carries cakes, pastries, pies, breads and rolls.
highlights: Home of the Ned Kelly pie
The Beesting is the other signature item
Cakes, pastries, pies, breads and rolls
On Camp Street in central Beechworth

name: Beechworth Coffee Roasters
description: A small batch coffee roaster on Boiler House Lane in Beechworth. Beans are sourced ethically and roasted in small batches into blends and single origins chosen to highlight the character of each bean, sold as whole bean or ground. They also supply cafes, offices and retailers wholesale and run a subscription delivery service.
highlights: Blends and single origins, whole bean or ground
Wholesale supply to cafes, offices and retailers

name: Beechworth Bakery Yackandandah
description: The Yackandandah shop of the Beechworth Bakery group, opened in 2017 on High Street in the middle of town. It sells the group's cakes, pastries, pies, breads and rolls including the Ned Kelly pie and the Beesting.
highlights: Cakes, pastries, pies, breads and rolls
On High Street in the town centre
Breakfast, lunch, snacks and early dinner
Closed Christmas Day and Boxing Day

name: Gum Tree Pies Yackandandah
description: The home store of Gum Tree Pies on High Street in Yackandandah, where the pies are made. The shop trades 8am to 4pm seven days and the business also sells online and at the Canberra market.
highlights: Pies made on site in Yackandandah
Also stalls at the Canberra market

name: White Owl Coffee Merchants
description: A family-owned specialty coffee roaster established in 2014 by Harry Perry to supply the Albury Wodonga region. Roasting is done on a 60kg Brambatti roaster at Fraser Road in Rutherglen. They sell beans, pods, subscriptions, brew equipment and merchandise, and supply cafes across the region including Valentine's Bakehouse.
highlights: Beans, pods, brew gear and subscriptions

name: Parker Pies
description: A pie shop on Main Street in Rutherglen making gourmet and traditional pies. It trades seven days, from 7.30am to 4.30pm Monday to Saturday and 7.30am to 4pm on Sunday, and closes on Good Friday, ANZAC Day, Christmas Day and Boxing Day.
highlights: Closed Good Friday, ANZAC Day, Christmas and Boxing Day

name: The Pickled Sisters Cafe
description: A family-run cafe and restaurant on Main Street in Rutherglen cooking homemade, locally sourced food. Daytime service runs Thursday to Monday from 10am to 3pm, with dinner Thursday to Saturday from 5.30pm and a pasta night on Thursdays. They also run cooking classes and sell picnic hampers, takeaway meals and catering for private functions.

name: Chiltern Bakery & Cafe
description: A bakery and cafe on Conness Street in Chiltern baking hand-shaped, stone-baked artisan breads and loaves. The counter also carries sausage rolls, pies, croissants and cakes, and the coffee is roasted in house. Catering platters and sandwich boxes can be ordered.

name: Thai Lotus
description: Thai Lotus is a family-owned Thai restaurant at the Botanic Gardens end of Dean Street in Albury. The kitchen serves traditional Thai cuisine across an extensive menu of curries, stir-fries and salads. Dine in, takeaway and delivery are all offered, with lunch and dinner service Tuesday to Saturday.
highlights: Lunch and dinner Tuesday to Saturday

name: Downtown Pizzeria
description: Downtown Pizzeria is a wood fired pizza and Italian restaurant on Dean Street, established in 2015. The menu covers pizzas, pastas, salads, entrees and sharing plates, with produce sourced locally. Vegan, gluten free and dairy free options are available, and the venue serves cocktails and local wines alongside dine in, takeaway and function bookings.
highlights: Vegan, gluten free and dairy free options
Wood fired pizza cooked at 472 Dean Street in the Albury CBD
Caters to dietaries including vegan, gluten free and dairy free

name: Level One Wine Bar
description: Level One Wine Bar is an upstairs wine bar and restaurant with bay windows looking over Dean Street. It stocks more than 300 wines on a wall-of-wine, with 15 or more available by the glass and the selection rotating every three weeks. Head chef Matt King runs a regularly updated seasonal menu built on fresh local produce, and the bar also pours beers and cocktails.
highlights: 15+ wines by the glass, rotating every three weeks
Seasonal menu by head chef Matt King
Beers and cocktails as well as wine

name: Indian Tandoori Restaurant Albury
description: Indian Tandoori Restaurant has been trading in Albury since 1998 and specialises in traditional North Indian and Goan cuisine. The menu changes from time to time and is cooked by qualified chefs from India, with tandoor baked meats and breads a focus. Lunch is served Tuesday to Sunday and dinner seven nights.
highlights: Opposite the cinema on Dean Street

name: Authentic Taste of India
description: Authentic Taste of India is a family owned restaurant on Dean Street next to the cinemas, run by Charanjit and Ramandeep Bhullar. The kitchen serves fare from northern India with an emphasis on tandoori dishes and curries made with fresh local produce. Dine in and takeaway are both available, with lunch service Thursday to Sunday.
highlights: Northern Indian tandoori dishes and curries
Next to the cinemas on Dean Street
Lunch Thursday to Sunday, dinner seven nights

name: Sen
description: Sen is a Vietnamese fine dining restaurant on Olive Street in central Albury. The menu draws on North, Central and South Vietnamese traditions using seasonal local ingredients and contemporary technique, with dishes such as Nha Trang cuttlefish and grilled pork jowl. Dinner is served Tuesday to Saturday from 5.30pm.
highlights: Dishes from North, Central and South Vietnam

name: Din Dins
description: Din Dins is an Asian fusion restaurant on Townsend Street in Albury, with a menu drawing on Chinese, Thai, Japanese and other Asian influences given a contemporary twist. Attached to the restaurant is the Panda Room, an 80 seat private function room with its own bar and kitchen. Lunch is served Wednesday to Saturday and dinner Tuesday to Saturday.
highlights: Panda Room private function space with its own bar
Cocktails, beer on tap and an extensive wine list

name: Vanilla Pod Pizza & Pasta Bar Albury
description: Vanilla Pod Pizza & Pasta Bar has been trading on Dean Street since 2018 as a family dining restaurant. The kitchen makes woodfired pizza and handmade pasta and also serves breakfast, premium steaks, seafood, desserts and kids' meals alongside coffee. Breakfast, lunch and dinner are served daily, with takeaway and online ordering available.

name: Canvas Eatery
description: Canvas Eatery sits behind the Murray Art Museum Albury overlooking QEII Square and has been trading since 2015. The kitchen runs a seasonal menu built around produce from the Riverina and Murray regions, and the room is a light filled space attached to the gallery. Specialty coffee is served alongside the food menu.

name: Taco Bill Albury
description: Taco Bill Albury is a Mexican restaurant on Dean Street serving tacos, enchiladas, fajitas, quesadillas and burritos. The venue is fully licensed and does not permit BYO. There is a children's menu plus vegan and coeliac options, and both dine in and takeaway are offered, with service from 5pm Wednesday to Sunday.

name: Thai Puka Restaurant
description: Thai Puka cooks Thai food drawn from the owners' childhood in Nan in northern Thailand, running true Thai favourites alongside evolving specials. The 85 seat restaurant is fully licensed with a wine list, beers and cocktails, and offers alfresco dining and air conditioning. Pad Thai noodles are the dish it is best known for, and vegetarian and gluten free options are available.
highlights: Cooking from Nan in northern Thailand
Fully licensed with wine, beer and cocktails

name: Indian Chimney
description: Indian Chimney has been on Dean Street since 2010 serving North Indian and regional Indian dishes, including clay oven baked breads. The menu covers entrees, mains, rice and naan and desserts with both vegetarian and non-vegetarian options. The venue has a refurbished dining area with outdoor seating, and offers in-store pickup plus local delivery to Albury, Wodonga and Thurgoona.
highlights: Delivery to Albury, Wodonga and Thurgoona

name: Albury Chinese Restaurant
description: Albury Chinese Restaurant serves standard Cantonese-style dishes and yum cha from an open dining room on Dean Street. Sizzling plates, beef dishes, dim sum and Peking duck feature on the menu, along with value meal packages. The restaurant is fully licensed and offers dine in, outdoor seating and takeaway.
highlights: Yum cha and Chinese à la carte
Sizzling plates, dim sum and Peking duck
Dine in, outdoor seating and takeaway

name: Baan Sabai Jai Thai Restaurant
description: Baan Sabai Jai has been serving Thai food on Smollett Street in Albury since 2009. The menu runs to traditional Thai curries and house specialties, with lunch service midweek and a Sunday daytime sitting. Dine in, pickup and delivery are all offered.

name: AIDA Mediterranean Cuisine & Bar
description: AIDA is a Mediterranean restaurant and bar on Dean Street in Albury cooking from traditional recipes. An outdoor charcoal grill drives much of the menu, which is built around chargrilled dishes and plates designed for sharing. Cocktails, a curated wine list and vegetarian options are also offered, with lunch and dinner Wednesday to Sunday.
highlights: Lunch and dinner Wednesday to Sunday

name: Argos Albury
description: Argos is a modern wood-fired Greek restaurant on Smollett Street in Albury. Cooking is done over a wood-fired charcoal oven using fresh ingredients, with a menu of shareable plates. Signature cocktails are served alongside the food.

name: South Albury Take Away
description: South Albury Take Away is a traditional fish and chip shop on Ebden Street that has been trading since 2000. Chips are hand cut from fresh potatoes, and the fish counter runs varieties including hake, flake and flounder plus other seafood. It opens early seven days a week.

name: Jones Street Take Away
description: Jones Street Take Away is a traditional fish and chip shop in Albury where the fish and battered products are made fresh rather than pre-battered. Beef patties are made in house from locally produced 100% Australian beef. The shop changes its frying oils regularly and trades six days a week, closed Tuesdays.

name: Borella Seafood
description: Borella Seafood has traded on Electra Street in East Albury since 1987 and runs three parts to the business. There is a fresh seafood counter selling fish fillets, prawns and oysters, a casual fish and chips takeaway, and Scales Restaurant serving contemporary seafood cooking. Stock is hand selected from Melbourne fishmongers.
highlights: Fresh fish, prawns and oysters counter
Stock hand selected from Melbourne fishmongers

name: Saigon Bites
description: Saigon Bites is a Vietnamese restaurant on Kiewa Street in Albury opened by Jess Nguyen and Tony Ngo. Pho and banh xeo have been the popular orders, alongside special fried rice, crispy egg noodles and sugar cane with rice noodles. The room seats around 60 including 36 outdoor seats on Kiewa Street, is fully licensed with cocktails, wines and tap beers, and offers takeaway.
highlights: Fully licensed with cocktails and tap beer

name: The Vietnamese Guy
description: The Vietnamese Guy is a casual licensed Vietnamese eatery on Dean Street in Albury with about 20 seats. The menu covers roast pork banh mi, pho, chicken bao buns, prawn spring rolls and Vietnamese iced coffee, and the kitchen is led by chef Jack. Delivery, takeaway and online ordering are available, with dairy free, gluten free, vegan and vegetarian choices.
highlights: Banh mi, pho and bao buns

name: Miss Amelie
description: Miss Amelie is a modern European restaurant set in the heritage former Wodonga railway station on Elgin Boulevard. The menu is offered as two or three courses plus a six course degustation midweek to Saturday, with vegan and gluten free menus available. An attached cocktail bar called Little Miss serves classic and contemporary drinks, and the venue takes private dining bookings and functions.
highlights: Housed in the heritage former Wodonga railway station
Two and three course menus plus six course degustation

name: Indian Tandoori Restaurant Wodonga
description: Indian Tandoori Restaurant Wodonga is the Stanley Street sibling of the Albury restaurant, trading under the same name since 1998. It cooks traditional North Indian and Goan cuisine, with poultry and meat curries, seafood, tikka and tandoor oven baked meats and breads. Banquets are available and dinner is served seven nights.
highlights: Sister restaurant to Indian Tandoori Albury

name: King of Curries
description: King of Curries is an Indian restaurant on Thomas Mitchell Drive in Wodonga specialising in North Indian cuisine. The menu uses fresh ingredients and authentic recipes with dishes drawn from different regions of India, including tandoori dishes and vegetarian and vegan options. Dinner is served Tuesday to Saturday from 5pm.
highlights: Dishes from different regions of India

name: Phaboonchai Thai Restaurant
description: Phaboonchai is a Thai restaurant on Beechworth Road in Wodonga, established in 2014. The menu covers stir fries, curries and rice dishes along with soups, noodles and salads. Online ordering, table reservations, pick-up and delivery are all offered.
highlights: Stir fries, curries and rice dishes

name: Casa 1872 Italian Ristorante
description: Casa 1872 is an Italian restaurant in a heritage-listed building on High Street in Wodonga, from the team behind Deli Bean Cafe and The Proprietor. The kitchen serves authentic Italian dishes and wood-fired pizza in a rustic dining room. Handcrafted pastas, locally sourced seafood, tiramisu, wine and espresso all feature, and the name refers to the building's history.
highlights: Authentic Italian cuisine and wood-fired pizza
Bookings by phone on 0433 038 660 or by email

name: Chao Thai Wodonga
description: Chao Thai has been trading on High Street in Wodonga since 2002. The restaurant serves a range of Thai dishes in a warm dining room with options for various dietary preferences. It caters for large group functions and takes reservations, with dinner served seven nights.

name: Real Thai Kitchen
description: Real Thai Kitchen has served Thai food on High Street in Wodonga since 2009. The dining room is set with white tablecloths and the kitchen is staffed by experienced chefs using traditional cooking techniques. Weekday lunch is served as well as dinner seven nights, and takeaway and home delivery are available.

name: Wodonga Noodle Canteen
description: Wodonga Noodle Canteen has been trading on High Street for more than 16 years. The menu runs to noodles, stir-fries and rice dishes, with gluten-free and vegetarian choices available. It is a licensed informal restaurant offering dine-in and takeaway, with street parking on High Street and disabled access.

name: La Maison
description: La Maison is a licensed cafe and restaurant on Lincoln Causeway at Gateway Island between Albury and Wodonga. The menu features grass fed steaks, fish, chicken, pork belly and pasta. Tapas, charcuterie and cheese platters and desserts are also served.

name: The Vietnamese Guy Wodonga
description: The Vietnamese Guy opened this High Street shop as a second location after demand from Wodonga locals travelling to the Albury store. The menu includes a selection of pho with both beef and chicken options. The shop is kid friendly with a small play pen, and serves lunch seven days with dinner Wednesday to Saturday.
highlights: Second location of the Albury original
Kid friendly with a small play pen

name: Junction Pizza
description: Junction Pizza is a locally owned and operated pizza, pasta and parmi takeaway shop on High Street in Wodonga. Snacks and desserts are also on the menu. There are sit-in options as well as takeaway.

name: Provenance
description: Provenance is a restaurant with accommodation on Ford Street in Beechworth, run by chef Michael Ryan. The kitchen leans Japanese and builds its tasting menu around local produce, served as bento-style courses made up of many individual plates. Dinner is served Friday to Monday.

name: Ford Street Enoteca
description: Ford Street Enoteca is a long-standing bistro in the centre of Beechworth serving relaxed Italian-leaning food. The kitchen works with fresh seasonal produce through house-made pasta and classic bistro dishes. The wine list is extensive, with a strong selection of local wines alongside international choices, and the room suits both small and larger groups.
highlights: Extensive local and international wine list

name: The Pickled Sisters Cafe + Restaurant
description: The Pickled Sisters is a family-run cafe and restaurant on Rutherglen's Main Street, a fixture in the town for more than 20 years. The kitchen cooks homemade food from locally sourced produce and matches it with regional wines. Brunch, long lunches, vineyard platters, takeaway meals and catering are offered, and Thursday night is pasta night.
highlights: Locally sourced produce and regional wines

name: Thousand Pound
description: Thousand Pound is a wine bar, store and restaurant on Rutherglen's Main Street. Executive chef Jack Cassidy cooks modern Australian food carrying Chinese, Thai, Vietnamese and Nepalese flavours, using produce from the business's own farms and regional growers. Local wines, creative cocktails and craft beers are poured alongside, with dinner Thursday to Saturday and bookings recommended.
highlights: Wine bar, wine store and restaurant
Local wines, cocktails and craft beer
Modern Australian cooking with Chinese, Thai, Vietnamese and Nepalese flavours
Wine bar and store on the same site

name: The Bended Elbow
description: A contemporary Australian styled hotel on Dean Street spread over two levels with multiple dining areas. There is a rooftop beer garden, a Melbourne-style alfresco laneway and a modern bistro, with a bar pouring tap beers, wines, spirits and cocktails. The venue runs live music and trivia nights and takes private function bookings.
highlights: Rooftop beer garden open Thursday to Saturday
Two-level venue with several dining areas
Tap beers, wines, spirits and cocktails

name: Sodens Hotel
description: A Wilson Street hotel with a family-friendly bistro, a sports bar and a beer garden. It has TAB, Keno and gaming facilities and a kids' play area, and runs live music on Friday and Saturday nights. Private function spaces include the Stable Bar, the Lounge and the Birdcage, used for birthdays, Christmas parties, business events, weddings and wakes.
highlights: Beer garden and kids' play area
Three function spaces: Stable Bar, Lounge and Birdcage

name: Commercial Club Albury
description: A large licensed club on Dean Street. Dining is spread across The Grill restaurant and Reflections Cafe, which serves breakfast and pastries from the club's own bakehouse, and there is a sports bar beside The Grill with multiple screens for sport and racing, TAB and Keno and an outdoor courtyard. The club also runs gaming promotions, artist shows and bands, a bottle shop, an on-site golf motel and sporting sections covering golf, lawn bowls, cue sports, squash and gym.
highlights: The Grill restaurant and Reflections Cafe
Sports bar with TAB, Keno and outdoor courtyard
Function rooms from board meetings to large events
Golf, lawn bowls, cue sports, squash and gym sections

name: SS&A Albury
description: The Albury Sailors, Soldiers and Airmen's Club on Olive Street, which traces its origins to a 1944 war services hall appeal. It has three bars with distinct identities: The Studio with free live entertainment on Friday and Saturday nights, the Aurum Lounge, and The Locker Room sports bar with giant screens and betting facilities. There is also a cafe and the Social Bar and Dining restaurant serving club and pub classics such as steaks, schnitzels and burgers alongside Asian dishes and a kids' menu, plus conference and function facilities and free on-site parking.
highlights: Three bars: The Studio, Aurum Lounge and The Locker Room
Free live entertainment Friday and Saturday nights
Sports bar with giant screens and betting facilities
Social Bar and Dining restaurant plus a cafe
Free on-site parking, wheelchair access via David Street

name: Albion Hotel
description: A Dean Street pub that has been part of the Albury CBD for over 100 years. The ground floor bistro serves pub-style counter meals and there is a rooftop bar upstairs for cocktails, spritzes and a grazing menu. The hotel also operates three function rooms and runs a bottomless brunch on Saturdays and Sundays.
highlights: Ground floor bistro with pub-style counter meals
Rooftop bar with cocktails and grazing menu

name: Public House Albury
description: A Dean Street pub serving contemporary pub food built on locally grown seasonal produce, alongside craft beers, regional wines and an extensive cocktail list that includes pre-order Cocktail Trees of twelve cocktails and frozen Poptails. Weekly regulars include happy hour from 4pm to 6pm daily, mini martinis on Wednesday evenings, two-for-one pizzas from noon on Thursdays and DJs from 9pm on Friday and Saturday. A kids menu is available and the venue takes function bookings.
highlights: Contemporary pub food from local seasonal produce
Craft beers, regional wines and an extensive cocktail list

name: Beer Deluxe Albury
description: A Kiewa Street pub that describes itself as Albury's home of entertainment, good times and cold beers. It has a beer garden, large screens showing live sport, a pub classics kitchen and a stage used for live music and touring acts. Trivia nights and function bookings are also offered.

name: Star Hotel
description: A Guinea Street hotel established in 1874 with a newly renovated public bar, a bistro, a sports bar and a beer garden. Carlton Draught tank beer is poured on site. Two function spaces, The Laneway and The Shed, are available for events.
highlights: Renovated public bar and sports bar
The Laneway and The Shed function spaces

name: Astor Hotel Albury
description: A Young Street hotel that describes its look as where retro meets modern. It combines a pub and bar with a food offering the Visit Albury Wodonga dining guide describes as pub style meals featuring a woodfire grill and rotisserie. The hotel also has accommodation, hosts live events and is used as a function and photoshoot venue.
highlights: Retro-styled hotel bar and dining room
Pub meals from a woodfire grill and rotisserie

name: Brady's Railway Hotel
description: A Smollett Street pub with a bistro serving pub food and contemporary Australian dishes, a beer garden, and a public bar showing live sport. There is a drive-through bottle shop open until midnight Monday to Saturday. Weekly regulars include raffles, trivia, music bingo, joker poker and a members draw, and the hotel has function facilities.
highlights: Bistro open for lunch daily and dinner nightly
Raffles, trivia, music bingo and joker poker

name: Dux Albury
description: A Dean Street bar and dining room offering curated wines, cocktails and share plates, with bar seating and intimate dining. Private event bookings can be made outside standard trading hours. Dux was named a Critics' Pick in the SMH Good Food Guide 2025.
highlights: Private event bookings outside standard hours
Critics' Pick, SMH Good Food Guide 2025

name: The Thirsty Devil Brewery
description: Independent brewery and bar on Townsend Street in South Albury with six core beers brewed on site: pale ale, IPA, red ale, mid strength ale, porter and ginger beer. Food comes from the Hungry Devil food van, which serves starters, finger food, burgers and kids options with gluten free selections. The venue runs Hoppy Hour specials, trivia, live music, open mic and jam nights, brewery tours and workshops.
highlights: Six core beers brewed on site: pale ale, IPA, red ale, mid strength ale, porter and ginger beer
Food served from the Hungry Devil food van, with gluten free selections
Function spaces for 30 to 100 guests, or 150 plus for the full venue
Dogs are welcome in the beer gardens if kept on a lead
Hoppy Hour Wednesday to Friday 4-6pm, plus trivia, live music and open mic nights
Hungry Devil food van at peak times

name: Boomerang Hotel
description: A Wagga Road hotel in Lavington with a family bistro serving pub fare, steaks and kids meals, a sports bar with TAB, and gaming facilities. Breakfast is served daily from 7.30am. The hotel has 38 motel rooms with ensuites, air-conditioning, TV and WiFi, an indoor pool, and function rooms used for birthdays, weddings and corporate events.
highlights: Family bistro with steaks and a kids menu

name: Kinross Woolshed
description: A hotel in Thurgoona set in a converted woolshed on a wide open site. It has a sports bar, a bistro, a beer garden and outdoor deck, and a gaming lounge, plus function spaces. The venue hosts live music and entertainment and is family friendly.

name: Jindera Hotel
description: A country pub in the centre of Jindera serving classic pub meals and drinks. It offers indoor and outdoor dining with a spacious beer garden and runs regular community events. Disabled access is available.
highlights: Country pub in the centre of Jindera

name: Howlong Golf Resort
description: A golf club and resort on Golf Club Drive at Howlong. Alongside the golf course it runs the Fairways Bistro, a pro shop, on-site resort accommodation and a functions venue. Separate contact lines are published for the pro shop, accommodation, bistro and memberships.

name: Club Corowa
description: The Corowa RSL club on Betterment Parade, trading as Club Corowa. It has a bistro and cafe with alfresco dining, a club lounge and the Silks sports bar serving cocktails, gourmet pizza and appetisers. Function spaces run across three levels and include a high-tech auditorium. The club also has indoor and outdoor playgrounds and an 18-hole Mini Golf on the Murray course, and runs a shuttle service from Thursday to Sunday between 5pm and close.
highlights: Bistro and cafe with alfresco dining
Function spaces across three levels plus an auditorium
Shuttle service Thursday to Sunday from 5pm

name: Wodonga RSL
description: An RSL club on Reid Street with The Fowlers Stove Bistro, which seats 100 inside plus an alfresco balcony, and a bar stocking local wines and Australian beverages. The club is pokie free and family friendly, welcoming veterans, families and the general public. Function rooms are available for hire and a courtesy bus runs Friday nights from 5pm to 9pm across local suburbs for a gold coin donation.
highlights: The Fowlers Stove Bistro, 100 seats plus alfresco balcony
Open on ANZAC Day and Remembrance Day

name: Blazing Stump Hotel
description: A family pub and dining venue on Anzac Parade that has operated on the site since 1880. It has a modern sports bar with the biggest sports screen in Wodonga, a large outdoor tank bar deck pouring brewery-fresh tank beer, a bottle shop open until late, and a 400 seat bistro that includes a Mountain deck looking out to the ranges.
highlights: Modern sports bar with the biggest sports screen in Wodonga
Outdoor tank bar deck with tank beer on tap

name: Huon Hill Hotel
description: A Reid Street pub and bistro in Wodonga. The bistro menu blends classic pub favourites with pizzas, gourmet burgers, salads and pub-style mains, and the venue publishes daily bistro specials and a live music line-up on its What's On page. Function bookings are taken and table bookings can be made online.
highlights: Bistro with pizzas, gourmet burgers, salads and pub mains

name: Church St Hotel
description: A hotel on Church Street in central Wodonga described in the Visit Albury Wodonga dining guide as a gastro pub serving contemporary cuisine and cocktails. The hotel's own site lists food and drink service, accommodation bookings, function facilities and special events.

name: The Lincoln
description: A gastro pub on Gateway Island at Wodonga, described in the Visit Albury Wodonga dining guide as having a cocktail lounge and beer garden. The venue serves casual bistro dining and offers large flexible indoor and outdoor spaces used for corporate functions, private events and weddings. Online bookings and gift cards are available.
highlights: Large indoor and outdoor function spaces

name: The Goods Shed
description: A bar and restaurant on Church Street, Wodonga running a seasonal menu and what it calls the largest craft beer fridge between Melbourne and Sydney. Pizza and fries are served daily between 3pm and 5pm. The venue takes online reservations and function bookings and sells gift vouchers.

name: Wodonga Golf Club
description: A golf club on Clubhouse Place set in a natural bush environment where native trees are a feature and Felltimber Creek runs through the layout. The course measures over 6,100 metres and is open daily except Christmas Day. On site are the Clubhouse Bar & Bistro, open Wednesday to Sunday for lunch and dinner with Sunday lunch, a lounge and spike bar, the only golf shop in Wodonga, and function and corporate event spaces.
highlights: Course over 6,100 metres in a bush setting
Felltimber Creek runs through the course
Clubhouse Bar & Bistro open Wednesday to Sunday

name: The Birallee Tavern
description: A locally owned tavern on Melrose Drive in Wodonga serving meals and drinks for occasions from casual lunches to celebrations. The venue has a dining room, a deck seating area, Bobby's Bar for cocktails and the Bira Bar gaming room, and hosts functions and events.

name: Tanswell's Hotel
description: A hotel built in 1853 on Ford Street in the centre of Beechworth. It has a front bar, a bandroom used for live music, and two levels of different dining areas. The kitchen serves lunch from noon to 2pm and dinner from 5.30pm to 8.30pm seven days, and the hotel takes accommodation and function bookings.
highlights: Built in 1853 in the centre of Beechworth

name: Bridge Road Brewers
description: Bridge Road Brewers has operated from a 150 year old coach house and stables in the centre of Beechworth since 2005. The taproom pours 20 house brewed beers on tap plus curated local wines, and the kitchen serves pizza. There is a sunny beer garden, a children's play area, complimentary bike hire and daily insider brewery tours. Beers include the Beechworth Pale Ale, Bling IPA, Little Hazy, alcohol free options and a ginger beer.
highlights: Set in a 150 year old coach house and stables
Beer garden and children's play area
Pizza served with the beer range

name: Star Hotel Yackandandah
description: A High Street pub first opened in 1863 and bought by Matt and Kim Frauenfelder in 2016, since restored with a renovated restaurant and beer garden. The kitchen centres on a fusion of southern USA and Australian barbecue with all meat smoked on the premises in hand-made smokers. The bar pours local beer through a partnership with Two Pot Brewing Co, gin and spirits from Yack Creek and Backwoods distilleries, and local wines and ciders. The pub is a live music venue and hosts a main stage for the Yackandandah Folk Festival and the Spring Migration Festival.
highlights: Local beer from Two Pot Brewing Co
Gin and spirits from Yack Creek and Backwoods distilleries
Live music venue and festival stage

name: Telegraph Hotel
description: A hotel on Conness Street in the middle of Chiltern's historic streetscape. The bistro serves parmigiana, pizzas, fish and chips, steaks and burgers, and the pub has a large beer garden and TAB. Friday nights bring community raffles, and happy hours run through the week.
highlights: In Chiltern's historic Conness Street streetscape
Bistro with parmigiana, pizza, steaks and burgers

name: The Victoria Hotel Rutherglen
description: A landmark heritage hotel on Rutherglen's Main Street redeveloped as an owner-operated boutique hotel, and awarded AHA Victoria's Best Redeveloped Hotel. The restaurant serves flame-focused cooking with an emphasis on local produce and lunch and dinner run seven days, with takeaway pizza also available. Accommodation is 14 king suites, some of them dog friendly, and there are event spaces for functions.
highlights: Heritage hotel on Rutherglen's Main Street
14 boutique king suites, select rooms dog friendly

name: Borella Butchery
description: Family run butcher on Borella Road in East Albury selling grass fed beef, Angus, Wagyu, Tasmanian lamb, pork and chicken. Smallgoods are made on site in wood fired smokers, and the counter also carries dry aged beef, sausages, BBQ rubs and sauces, chef prepared meals and pastry items. Free local delivery is offered.
highlights: Smallgoods made on site in wood fired smokers
Grass fed beef, Angus and Wagyu

name: Locky's Countryside Meats
description: Butcher shop on Macauley Street in Albury stocking beef, pork, lamb and chicken. It carries a large selection of continental smallgoods including hams, salami and smoked meats, and supplies halal meat in a range of quantities. Retail and commercial packs are available with delivery.
highlights: Continental smallgoods, hams, salami and smoked meats

name: Wolki Butchery
description: Self serve butchery on Urana Road selling grass fed and pasture raised beef, lamb and pork from Wolki Farm. The shop describes itself as Australia’s first 24/7 self serve butchery, with access open around the clock to members. Membership is free but places are limited.
highlights: Self serve butchery open 24/7 to members
Grass fed and pasture raised beef, lamb and pork

name: Arnold's Fruit Market
description: Fruit and vegetable market on Osburn Street in Wodonga that also carries meat, groceries, bakery, dairy and confectionery. The business traces back to 1892 when J.G Arnold began selling fresh fruit and vegetables in Albury and is now in its fifth generation of family ownership. An online shop and delivery service covers Albury Wodonga and surrounding areas, and Brian’s Nursery operates within the store.
highlights: Trading since 1892, five generations of family ownership
Fresh fruit and vegetables plus groceries, meat, bakery and dairy
Online shop with delivery around Albury Wodonga

name: Miss Amelie Gourmet
description: A gourmet food business with its Wodonga shop at 6 Michael Drive, alongside outlets in Albury, Beechworth and two Melbourne markets. Miss Amelie Gourmet sells pies, pastries and desserts, heat-and-eat meals, deli and seafood lines, pantry goods and wine, and offers catering.
highlights: Pies, pastries, desserts and heat-and-eat meals
Deli, seafood, pantry goods and wine
Pies medalled in Australia's Best Pie Competition 2021, 2022 and 2023
Catering delivered or available to collect
Wodonga shop open Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 4.30pm
Pies, heat and eat meals and desserts

name: Cellar Door Wine Store
description: Boutique wine retailer and wine bar on the main street of Beechworth. It stocks an extensive selection of boutique Beechworth wines along with imported and rare wines and a range of spirits from around the world.
highlights: Wine bar as well as retail store
On Ford Street in the town centre

name: Olive Health Foods
description: Health food store on Olive Street that describes itself as the largest health food store between Melbourne and Sydney. It stocks vitamins, minerals and herbs, natural makeup and skincare, water filters, eco friendly and allergy friendly products, local products and sports supplements. An in house clinic offers naturopathic consultations, allergy and intolerance testing and seminars.
highlights: Allergy friendly and eco friendly products

name: A Zesty Health
description: Health food shop on High Street Wodonga stocking organic, eco friendly and chemical free products alongside supplements and whole foods. Lines include nuts, seeds, legumes, grains, herbs and spices, dried fruit, sourdough bread, protein powders, essential oils, medicinal mushroom powders and skincare, with a focus on plant based, gluten free and dairy free diets. Nutrition consultations are also offered.
highlights: Bulk nuts, seeds, grains, herbs and spices
Gluten free, dairy free and plant based lines

name: Wholefoods
description: Organic grocery store on Romet Road in Wodonga stocking organic fresh produce, pantry staples, bread, eggs, frozen food, home and cleaning products, beauty items, beverages, wellness supplements, baby and kids products and pet food. Click and collect is available, and there is a second store in Wangaratta.

name: BOOKtique Albury
description: Independent bookshop in AMP Lane off Dean Street, Albury. Stock is spread across more than 60 categories including fiction, children’s books, crime and thrillers and science fiction, alongside journals, cards and gifts. Audiobooks are sold through a Libro.fm partnership.
highlights: Children’s books, crime and science fiction

name: Thistle & Fern
description: Florist with a shop in South Albury and a second location at Junction Square in Wodonga, selling seasonal fresh flowers, arrangements, gifts and greeting cards. Deliveries run Tuesday to Friday, with a flat delivery rate covering Wodonga, Albury, Lavington, Glenroy, Springdale Heights, Hamilton Valley, Thurgoona, Killara and Bandiana.
highlights: Shops in South Albury and Junction Square Wodonga
Flat rate delivery across Albury Wodonga suburbs
Florist shop in South Albury, open Tuesday to Friday 8.30am to 5pm
Flowers and greeting cards, with a hand-written card on orders
Same-day delivery Tuesday to Friday for orders placed before 12pm

name: Jannoel Floral Co.
description: Florist on High Street in Wodonga selling fresh flower bouquets and arrangements for a range of occasions, with delivery across Albury Wodonga and a same day delivery option.

name: Peards Nursery Albury
description: Garden centre at the Peards site on Borella Road, Albury, selling plants, trees, pots and water features alongside giftware and homewares. The nursery opens every day from 8:00am and there is a cafe on site serving coffee and meals.

name: Peards Nursery Wodonga
description: Nursery on Elgin Boulevard in Wodonga carrying a large range of indoor and outdoor shrubs, trees and seedlings, plus garden giftware and accessories. The business has been locally owned and operating for more than 40 years.
highlights: Indoor and outdoor shrubs, trees and seedlings

name: Our Native Garden Nursery
description: Nursery supplying native plants local to the Albury Wodonga region for revegetation projects, landscaping and home gardens, propagated from locally sourced seed. It sits next to the Re-use Shop at the Wodonga Transfer Station, with parking at the Re-use Shop, and opens Friday mornings and Saturday middays.
highlights: Indigenous plants local to the Albury Wodonga region
Stock for revegetation, landscaping and home gardens
Next to the Re-use Shop at Wodonga Transfer Station

name: Comet Cycles
description: Bike shop on Dean Street, Albury selling road, mountain, gravel, fitness, kids and e-bikes along with parts and cycling accessories. The workshop handles everything from tune ups to custom builds, aiming to complete repairs on the spot where possible and quoting in advance otherwise.
highlights: Road, mountain, gravel, fitness and e-bikes
Shopfront at 2/435 Dean Street in the Albury CBD
Stocks Trek, Specialized, Giant and BMC bicycles
Separate sales and service contacts: bikes@cometcycles.com.au and service@cometcycles.com.au

name: Border Bikes AW
description: Bike shop on Chapple Street, Wodonga handling sales, servicing and repairs. It is a stockist for major bike brands and offers tune ups, custom part fitting, personal bike fitting, spare parts and help with delivery or pick up of bikes. The business started in 2014 as Cycle Station in the Albury CBD.

name: Adventure Gear Albury
description: Outdoor shop on Dean Street, Albury stocking hiking, camping and travel gear. Departments cover apparel, footwear, packs and bags, hydration, nutrition, navigation, optics and lighting, and repair and survival gear. Brands carried include Osprey, Fjällräven, Icebreaker, La Sportiva, Rab, Patagonia, Helinox, Lowa and Exped.
highlights: Brands include Osprey, Fjällräven, Icebreaker and Rab
On Dean Street in central Albury

name: Great Outdoors Albury
description: Outdoor and heating store on Wagga Road, Lavington selling barbecues and pizza ovens, wood heaters and gas heaters, outdoor furniture and umbrellas, camping equipment and prospecting gear, plus gas bottle refills. It is a Weber specialist dealer and calls itself the Border’s wood heater specialists.

name: All Music Direct
description: Musical instrument shop on Dean Street, Albury selling acoustic, electric, bass and classical guitars, amplifiers, keyboards and pianos, orchestral and folk instruments and drums. It also carries studio and live equipment including microphones, mixers, cables and audio interfaces, and has a guitar technician on staff.

name: Art Parts Fine Arts Supplies
description: Art supply shop on David Street, Albury stocking acrylic, gouache, oil and watercolour paint, stretched canvas, boards and rolls, mediums, brushes, easels, drawing tools, printmaking supplies, paper and journals. The shop also runs creative workshops and sells gift certificates.

name: Gemglow Jewellers
description: Family jewellers in the City Walk Arcade off Dean Street, Albury, established in 1961. The business specialises in handmade bespoke jewellery, jewellery repairs and gifts, and carries pearl and silver jewellery.
addressLine: Shop 10, City Walk Arcade, 515-519 Dean Street
highlights: In City Walk Arcade off Dean Street

name: Armadio Style Collective
description: Women’s fashion boutique on Olive Street, Albury stocking mid to high end clothing and accessories, including dresses, tops, bottoms, outerwear, jewellery, bags, footwear and scarves. The store also sells online.
highlights: Mid to high end women’s clothing
Shop on Olive Street plus online store

name: Beechworth Emporium
description: Department store on Camp Street in Beechworth selling men’s and ladies clothing, accessories and footwear. It has traded for over 30 years and occupies a building dating back to the 1850s, describing itself as today’s department store with yesteryear’s service.
highlights: Men’s and ladies clothing, accessories and footwear
On Camp Street in central Beechworth

name: 2 Grey Birds
description: Family owned gift store on Olive Street, Albury describing itself as a treasure trove of gifts, curated hampers, homewares, paper goods and cards. Ranges cover cards, baby and wedding gifts and homewares, with a focus on independent designers and home grown brands.
highlights: Stocks independent designers and Australian brands

name: The Yack Store
description: Shop on High Street in Yackandandah described as an old fashioned emporium with the latest books and gifts. It stocks books, including classic Little Golden Books, and gifts for a range of occasions.
highlights: On High Street in central Yackandandah

name: Giftwrapt Corowa
description: Gift shop on Sanger Street in Corowa selling giftware, hampers and gift vouchers.

name: Who What Why
description: Toy and gift shop on Dean Street, Albury trading under the line "an education in toys". It has been locally owned and operated since 1995 and stocks over 3000 items covering educational toys, games, puzzles, craft supplies and children’s gifts, with brands including Connetix, Schleich, Melissa & Doug and Ravensburger.
highlights: Brands include Connetix, Schleich and Ravensburger
Gifts from baby age up to teenagers
Over 3000 items in stock across toys, games, puzzles and craft
Stocks Melissa & Doug, Schleich, Playmobil, Ravensburger, Brio and Jellycat

name: Blairs Produce
description: Rural and livestock supplies store on Wagga Road, Lavington. It carries pet food and animal health products, crop protection chemicals and seed, veterinary supplies, produce, garden lines and general merchandise, stocking brands including AgBoss, Blundstone and Bainbridge.
highlights: Retail produce store at 341 Wagga Rd, Lavington
Pet food, veterinary products and garden supplies

name: Parkside Produce
description: Family owned produce store on Osburn Street, Wodonga supplying stock feed, equine and poultry products, farm supplies and domestic pet food. The store has a drive through, which it describes as the only one in the region.

name: Kellys Mitre 10
description: Locally owned family run hardware store on Elgin Boulevard, Wodonga. It runs a trade centre carrying building materials, is an authorised STIHL dealer for sales and servicing with genuine parts, and stocks rural and animal care products plus workwear and boots. Local delivery and equipment servicing are offered to builders, tradespeople and farmers across the Albury Wodonga region.

name: Rutherglen Home Hardware
description: Independent hardware store on Main Street, Rutherglen carrying a range of home improvement and hardware products for home and weekend projects, with in store shopping, delivery and same day service options.

name: Leather & Thread
description: Furniture store at the corner of Romet Road and McKoy Street in West Wodonga, selling lounges, dining settings, bedroom suites, living room furniture and outdoor ranges. The site also houses Good Night Sleep and La-Z-Boy Albury Wodonga.
highlights: Good Night Sleep bedding on site

name: Whatever Where-ever Craft
description: Patchwork, quilting and sewing shop in Howlong stocking over 2,000 bolts of fabric across brights, florals, reproductions and children’s prints. It also carries patterns, pre-cuts such as jelly rolls, layer cakes and charm squares, kits, books, templates, felt, yarn and notions, and sells online.
highlights: Pre-cuts including jelly rolls and charm squares
Online store as well as shopfront

name: Johnsons MME Accountants and Advisors
description: Johnsons MME is an accounting and advisory firm with offices in Albury and Wangaratta. Services listed include accounting, taxation, audit and assurance, financial advisory, finance strategy, SMSF specialists, succession planning and business performance coaching. The firm also lists fuel tax credit reviews, sustainable business services and biodiversity services, and runs client portals for collaboration and financial advisory.

name: Harris Lieberman
description: Harris Lieberman is a law firm that has practised in the Albury-Wodonga region since 1886, with its office at 87 Hume Street, Wodonga. Practice areas listed are commercial law, wills and estate planning, property and conveyancing, family law, employment law and personal injury including workers compensation. The firm states it is part of the Sather Legal Group.

name: McHargs Solicitors
description: McHargs Solicitors was established in 1930 and practises from 81 High Street in central Wodonga, serving clients in both Victoria and New South Wales. The firm handles residential, commercial and farming conveyancing, property law matters such as easements, covenants, caveats, title matters and leasing, and property development work including subdivisions, re-zonings and planning permits. It also prepares wills, powers of attorney and administers deceased estates.
highlights: Property development, subdivisions and planning permits
Wills, powers of attorney and deceased estates
Practises in both Victoria and NSW

name: Pogson Cronin Kerr Solicitors & Notary
description: PCK Solicitors, trading as Pogson Cronin Kerr Solicitors & Notary, is a general law firm based on Urana Road in Lavington. Listed practice areas are conveyancing, property law, business and commercial, civil litigation, criminal law, family law, deceased estates and wills and estate planning. The firm also provides notary public services.
highlights: General practice firm serving the cross-border region
Wills, estate planning and deceased estates

name: ACH Legal
description: ACH Legal, formerly Keating Avery Solicitors, is a full-service law firm at 72 High Street, Wodonga, acting for clients in Victoria and New South Wales. Practice areas listed are property and conveyancing, wills and estates, family law, criminal law, business and company law, and civil litigation.

name: Robb & Associates Solicitors
description: Robb & Associates Solicitors is a family law practice on Smollett Street in Albury. Listed areas of work include divorce, family law property settlements, de facto property settlements, children's matters, child support, binding financial agreements and surrogacy. The firm offers Skype and electronic appointments as well as in-person meetings.
highlights: Property settlements and de facto matters

name: Sargeants Wodonga
description: Sargeants Wodonga is the Wodonga branch of the Sargeants conveyancing network, operating from 85 High Street. The practice describes itself as property transfer specialists, handling conveyancing for real estate transactions.
highlights: Part of the Sargeants conveyancing network

name: Mortgage Finance Solutions
description: Mortgage Finance Solutions is a mortgage and finance broking firm on Stanley Street in Wodonga, also serving Albury, Wangaratta and Yarrawonga Mulwala. The business is split into residential lending for first home buyers, investors and refinancing, asset finance for plant, equipment and vehicles, and commercial finance for property investment, business acquisitions and capital funding. It states relationships with more than 30 lenders and full membership of the Mortgage and Finance Association of Australia.
highlights: First home buyer and refinancing loans
Residential lending for first home buyers, investors and refinancing
Asset finance for plant, equipment and vehicles
Commercial finance for property investment and business acquisitions

name: Swift Finance Brokers
description: Swift Finance Brokers is a mortgage broking firm on Swift Street in Albury serving the Albury and Wodonga area. Listed services cover new home loans for first-time buyers, investment property finance, mortgage refinancing, asset and equipment finance, and loan protection. The brokerage says it sources deals from a panel of over 40 lenders.
highlights: First home buyer and investment loans

name: PRD Albury
description: PRD Albury is a licensed real estate office on Swift Street serving the Albury-Wodonga region across NSW and Victoria. The office handles residential sales, property management, rentals and leasing, and commercial property.
highlights: Covers both NSW and Victorian sides of the border

name: Century 21 Twin City
description: Century 21 Twin City is a real estate office on Dean Street in Albury. The office handles residential sales and purchases, rental property management, market appraisals for sellers, rental appraisals and open inspections.

name: Elders Real Estate Wodonga
description: Elders Real Estate Wodonga operates from Stanley Street in Wodonga, with a companion office at Howlong. The agency covers residential sales and rentals, commercial property sales and leasing, property management, storage shed rentals, and market appraisals and property reports.

name: Pollock Architecture
description: Pollock Architecture is an architectural practice on Dean Street in Albury servicing Albury-Wodonga and the surrounding region. The practice publishes a portfolio of residential projects. highlights: Google Ads and Meta ads management

The centre also produces signage including A-frames, pull-up banners, window decals and corflute signs, and offers graphic design such as logo and brochure design.
highlights: Pull-up banners, A-frames and corflute signs

Work covers building signage, digital, LED and neon signs, pylon and free-standing signs, vehicle wraps, engraving, fabrication and letter bending, safety, traffic and reflective signs, and line marking. The workshop runs a UV flatbed printer able to print onto cardboard, glass, timber, plastic and metal, and also does glass frosting and tinting, wall graphics and wallpaper. The business is a member of the Australian Sign & Graphics Association and runs a corflute recycling program.
highlights: UV flatbed printing onto glass, timber, plastic and metal

name: Corowa Signs
description: Corowa Signs is a signwriting and digital printing business on Honour Avenue in Corowa, servicing Albury-Wodonga and surrounding districts with over 30 years of experience. The business designs, manufactures and installs retail and corporate signage, vehicle signage and wraps, decals, banners and stickers, plaques, gold leaf lettering and traffic signs. highlights: Gold leaf lettering and hand-painted signs

name: Cameron Dental Care

name: Wodonga Family Dental

highlights: Dental fillings, extractions and root canal treatments

The clinic also runs group programs including GLA:D, a resistance class, RUN HUB and an adolescent class.
highlights: GLA:D and RUN HUB group programs

Chiropractic adjustments and remedial massage therapy

Glaucoma screening and visual field testing
Children's eye exams from age three

General services cover health checks, vaccinations, microchipping, surgery, desexing and dentistry, and the practice also lists advanced imaging, laser therapy, hydrotherapy and radioactive iodine therapy for cats. Visiting specialists in dermatology, ophthalmology and surgery attend, and the clinic runs a mobile vet service, a blood bank and an adoption program. It is on call for emergencies 24/7.

Visiting dermatology, ophthalmology and surgical specialists

highlights: Long day care from six weeks to six years
