highlights: 12 acres of bushland on the Murray River

name: Heritage Motor Inn Corowa
description: A motor inn on Edward Street in central Corowa with Deluxe Queen, Deluxe Twin, Superior Queen, Superior Twin and Superior King rooms, an Executive King Spa, a two bedroom apartment and an executive three bedroom apartment. The site notes dining, EV charging and its central location, with direct booking available through the website.
highlights: Rooms from deluxe queen through to a 3 bedroom apartment

name: Federation Motel Resort
description: A motel resort on Honour Avenue at Corowa, across the Murray River from the Rutherglen wine district. The property advertises the biggest motel rooms in Corowa, with newly refurbished Standard Family, Executive King and Spa rooms. Facilities are a salt water swimming pool and spa, a guest barbecue in a shady garden area, guest laundry, free wireless internet and ample parking for trailers, large vehicles, buses and boats.
highlights: Salt water swimming pool and spa
Guest BBQ in a shady garden area
Parking for buses, boats and large vehicles
Guest laundry and free wireless internet
Across the river from the Rutherglen wine district

name: Yackandandah Holiday Park
description: A holiday park within walking distance of the historic Yackandandah town centre, offering self-contained cabins plus powered and unpowered camping sites for caravans and tents. Facilities include shower and toilet amenities, a guest laundry, camp kitchen, free BBQs and free WiFi, with linen and towels supplied in cabins. Sites are grassy and shaded, and the park is dog friendly subject to conditions.
highlights: Walking distance to Yackandandah town centre
Self-contained cabins with linen and towels
Powered and unpowered grassy shaded sites

name: Golden Heritage Accommodation
description: Motel and self-contained accommodation on Sydney Road, about two minutes' drive or a 15 minute walk from the Beechworth village centre. Options are Executive King Suites and Deluxe Queen motel rooms, one and two bedroom self-contained spa cottages and two bedroom self-contained apartments. Rooms include free WiFi, quality linen, microwaves, pod coffee machines, LCD smart TVs and heating and air-conditioning, and elevated verandas look over historic Beechworth. EV charging is offered to guests who book direct, and cycling facilities are available.
highlights: Self-contained one and two bedroom spa cottages
Executive king suites and deluxe queen rooms
EV charging for direct booking guests
Pod coffee machines and microwaves in rooms
15 minute walk to the Beechworth village centre

name: Beechworth Cabins
description: Self-contained cabin accommodation on High Street in Beechworth. The cabin has two bedrooms, one with a double bed and one with triple bunks, a bathroom with shower, a lounge area and a kitchenette with a stovetop and full-size refrigerator and freezer. The site describes Beechworth as a rustic escape known for its gold mining heritage, galleries, craft breweries and fine dining.
highlights: Triple bunks in the second bedroom
Kitchenette with stovetop and full-size fridge freezer

name: Beechworth House
description: Guest accommodation on Dingle Road, Beechworth, with three suites named Le Tour, Citron and Jardin. Gourmet dinners are prepared nightly by chef Denis Hagger using food sourced from the on-site gardens, local orchards and direct from growers. A guest program includes complimentary champagne on arrival, daily continental breakfast, a chef's welcome treat and discounted wine selections. The property is dog friendly.
highlights: Gourmet dinners prepared nightly on site
Produce from on-site gardens and local orchards

name: The Inn Beechworth
description: Three self-contained cottages for short-term accommodation in Beechworth. Kelly House is a restored 1890s property with three bedrooms, each with its own private bathroom, soft European linens and an open fire. Picketts Cottage is a smaller cottage for two with a clawfoot tub and a cosy lounge, and Ned's Nook is a studio suited to solo travellers or couples. The properties are described as having old-world character with modern comforts, and pets are welcome.
highlights: Restored 1890s Kelly House with three ensuite bedrooms
Picketts Cottage with a clawfoot tub
Ned's Nook studio for solo travellers or couples

name: Rutherglen Country Cottages
description: A bed and breakfast run by hosts Alister and Heather Chisholm, with entry via the rear on Murray Street opposite the golf course. GumTree Cottage has one bedroom with a queen bed, ensuite, air conditioning and a separate living area, and Garden Cottage has two bedrooms with two queen beds, ensuite, air conditioning and two separate toilets. Guests have a swimming pool and an alfresco area with BBQ, fridge, fire and television, and breakfast is included. The cottages are a five minute walk to the shopping centre, restaurants and pubs, adjacent to an 18-hole golf course and near the 1.2km walking track around Lake King.
highlights: Alfresco area with BBQ, fridge and fire
Five minute walk to Rutherglen shops and restaurants

name: Motel Woongarra
description: A motel on Drummond Street about 0.5km from the Rutherglen town centre and around 30 minutes' drive from Albury Wodonga. Room types are Supreme King, Supreme Queen, Twin and Family Suite, all spacious ground floor rooms with smart televisions, reverse cycle air conditioning, microwave, bar fridge, kettle, toaster and iron. The property has an outdoor swimming pool, a BBQ area with outdoor seating, free on-site parking and free WiFi, and a high chair and portable cot are available on request.
highlights: Family suite with high chair and cot on request
Free on-site parking and free WiFi

name: The Gatta Inn
description: A motel on the shores of Lake Hume at Tallangatta, formerly trading as the Tallangatta Motor Inn. It positions itself as a bike friendly motel and is developing cycling amenities including secure bike storage, repair stations and cycling route maps for guests. Bike shuttle services to scenic trailheads are offered, equipped to carry multiple bikes and bookable one-way or return. The office is open 10am to 5pm and online booking is available.
highlights: Secure bike storage and repair stations
On the shores of Lake Hume

name: Murray Art Museum Albury (MAMA)
description: MAMA is Albury's public art museum on Dean Street, showing rotating exhibitions by local, international and First Nations artists. Entry is free and the museum is open seven days a week, 362 days of the year. The building also holds a store of Australian design, the Canvas Eatery, and the MAMA Studio art class and workshop program.
highlights: Rotating exhibitions of local, international and First Nations artists
MAMA Studio art classes and workshops
Museum store and Canvas Eatery on site
Closed Anzac Day, Good Friday and Christmas

name: Albury LibraryMuseum
description: A combined public library and museum run by AlburyCity on the corner of Kiewa and Swift Streets. It runs a changing exhibition program of touring exhibitions, works from the AlburyCity Collection and community shows, alongside the permanent exhibitions 'Crossing Place: A Story of Albury' and 'Sharing Bonegilla Stories'. Admission is free, and there are public computers, local history resources and study and meeting rooms for hire.
highlights: Permanent exhibition 'Crossing Place: A Story of Albury'
Local history collections and public computers
Study and meeting rooms for hire

name: Albury Botanic Gardens
description: AlburyCity's botanic gardens sit on the corner of Dean and Smollett Streets, with the main entrance gates on Wodonga Place. The grounds hold established trees, meandering pathways and colourful garden beds, and visitors are invited to picnic on the lawns and watch for native wildlife. There is a separate Children's Garden, accessible parking and accessible toilets, and paths that suit mobility aids and powered wheelchairs.
highlights: Free entry, open daily from 6:30am to sunset
Children's Garden open 8:30am to sunset, closed Wednesdays outside NSW school holidays
Established trees, pathways and garden beds

name: Monument Hill
description: Monument Hill is Albury's most prominent viewing point, at the western end of Dean Street and reached via Memorial Drive. On top stands the Albury and District War Memorial, a 100-foot reinforced concrete obelisk unveiled on Anzac Day 1925 and paid for by public subscription. The surrounding bushland reserve has walking tracks, picnic tables, seating, a drinking fountain, public toilets and commemorative plaques, and wildflowers including terrestrial orchids appear in spring and summer.
addressLine: Memorial Drive, western end of Dean Street
highlights: Free public reserve with views over Albury and the region
Albury and District War Memorial, unveiled Anzac Day 1925
Picnic tables, seating and drinking fountain
Site of the annual Anzac Day ceremony

name: Wonga Wetlands
description: Wonga Wetlands is an 80 hectare system of seven lagoons on the Murray River floodplain downstream from Albury, created using treated water from the city. More than 154 bird species have been identified here and six bird hides are spread around the lagoons. Walking trails of 0.5km, 1.2km and 2.5km start near the visitors centre, and the site includes an Indigenous Wiradjuri campsite with a cooking area, sleeping area, rock art displays and a ceremonial dancing circle.
highlights: Seven lagoons across 80 hectares of Murray River floodplain
Six bird hides and more than 154 recorded bird species
Wiradjuri campsite with rock art displays and ceremonial dancing circle
Connects to the Wagirra Trail and Yindyamarra Sculpture Walk

name: Nail Can Hill
description: Nail Can Hill is a 1200 hectare bushland reserve on the western edge of Albury, holding about 5km of walking trails and 29km of mountain bike trails across roughly 70 individual tracks. The Ridge Trail is the longest walk at 7.9km, with shorter marked routes such as Bakes Trail (2.18km) and Pete's Trail (2.47km). Vegetation includes Box Gum Grassy Woodland, Granitic Hills Woodland, Heath Dry Forest and Box Ironbark Forest, and the reserve has hosted the Nail Can Hill Run since 1977. The main car park is on Range Road, with limited parking at Roper Street, Centaur Road and Pemberton Street.
highlights: Free access to 1200 hectares of bushland
About 29km of mountain bike singletrack across roughly 70 tracks
5km of walking trails including the 7.9km Ridge Trail
Main car park and information board on Range Road
Downloadable track maps and trail notes
Home of the annual Nail Can Hill Run since 1977

name: Wagirra Trail and Yindyamarra Sculpture Walk
description: The Wagirra Trail is an 8.5km two metre wide shared pathway that links Horseshoe Lagoon with the South Albury Trail at the Union Bridge, running beside the Murray River through Noreuil, Australia and Hovell Tree parks and past the Oddies Creek playspace and Albury Swim Centre. The 5.3km section from Kremur Street to Wonga Wetlands is sealed and forms the Yindyamarra Sculpture Walk, lined with fifteen sculptures by local Aboriginal artists. Barbecues, picnic tables, public toilets and bins are spaced along the route.
highlights: Free 8.5km shared walking and cycling path beside the Murray River
Fifteen sculptures by local Aboriginal artists on the Yindyamarra Sculpture Walk
Sealed 5.3km section from Kremur Street to Wonga Wetlands
Passes Noreuil, Australia and Hovell Tree parks
Barbecues, picnic tables and public toilets along the trail

name: Noreuil Park Foreshore
description: Noreuil Park is a riverside park on Noreuil Parade, less than a kilometre from the Albury CBD off Wodonga Place. It has mature shade trees, large grassed areas, picnic and barbecue facilities and a fenced children's playground, plus a cafe kiosk, public toilets and showers. The park is a launching point for canoeing and kayaking on the Murray and a hub for the Wagirra Trail and Bungambrawatha Bike Trail.
highlights: Free riverside park a short walk from the Albury CBD
Cafe kiosk, public toilets and showers
Canoe and kayak access to the Murray River
On the Wagirra Trail and Bungambrawatha Bike Trail

name: Oddies Creek Park Adventure Playspace
description: Albury's largest playground, a 2,000 square metre fully fenced playspace set among mature gum trees off Ebden Street in South Albury and designed by Mary Jeavons. It includes a 30 metre flying fox, a giant bird nest swing, a complex climbing net, and two timber structures - a five metre high building with wheelchair accessible ramps and a smaller one for younger children with slides, climbers, rockers and a sandpit. Barbecues, picnic tables, shelter, seating, public toilets and a drinking fountain are on site, along with a leash free dog area.
highlights: Free, fully fenced 2,000 square metre playspace
30 metre flying fox and giant bird nest swing
Wheelchair accessible ramps on the main play structure
Separate junior play area with sandpit
Barbecues, picnic tables, shelter and public toilets

name: Regent Cinemas Albury
description: Regent Cinemas is Albury's cinema complex on Dean Street, offering several different auditorium types. Gold Class has reclining armchairs and personal call buttons for waiter service, RMAX is billed as the largest screen in regional Australia and runs a 4K laser projector, Regent Junior has a dedicated play area at the back of the cinema for kids, and Regent Lounge occupies the lower section of the heritage theatre with 32 double seated couches.
highlights: Gold Class cinemas with reclining armchairs and waiter service
RMAX, the largest screen in regional Australia, with 4K laser projection
Regent Junior with a play area inside the cinema
Regent Lounge with 32 double couches in the heritage theatre
In the centre of Albury on Dean Street

name: Albury Swim Centre
description: An outdoor swim centre on Wodonga Place owned by AlburyCity and operated by Aligned Leisure. The site has 50 metre pools, waterslides, lifeguards on duty, a kiosk and picnic and barbecue facilities, and runs learn to swim and kids' programs. Opening hours change with the season, so check the operator's hours page before visiting.
highlights: Outdoor 50 metre pools with lifeguards on duty
Kiosk plus picnic and barbecue facilities
Learn to swim and kids' programs

name: Lavington Swim Centre
description: A seasonal outdoor swimming pool on Moore Street, Lavington, owned by AlburyCity and operated by Aligned Leisure. It opens over the summer months with swimming programs, lifeguards on duty, a kiosk and picnic and barbecue facilities, and hosts low cost aqua exercise classes.
highlights: Seasonal outdoor pool open over summer
Swimming programs and low cost aqua exercise classes
Kiosk plus picnic and barbecue facilities

name: Worlds Beyond
description: Worlds Beyond on Urana Road, Lavington runs virtual reality escape rooms and other immersive experiences, including Quest Boxes, PixaPlay and party packages, along with educational content experiences. Online bookings close two hours before a session and the venue asks people to call for shorter notice, as staff are rostered on confirmed bookings and walk ins are not guaranteed. Gift vouchers are available.
highlights: Booking strongly recommended, walk ins not guaranteed

name: Table Top Reserve
description: A quiet AlburyCity reserve north of Thurgoona overlooking the Bowna arm of Lake Hume, Table Top Nature Reserve and Budgingi Trig Station Hill. It has Lake Hume water frontage when the lake is full, though water access recedes quickly as levels drop, and there is no direct vehicle access to the water. Facilities are a small playground, picnic tables, a public toilet and seating under mature shade trees, and much of the reserve has been revegetated.
highlights: Free reserve with views over the Bowna arm of Lake Hume
No direct vehicle access to the water

name: Lake Hume
description: Lake Hume sits about 20 kilometres east of the Albury CBD and is one of Australia's most important water storages, its dam completed in 1936 when it was the largest in the southern hemisphere. Four parks give public access to the water: Table Top Reserve, Bowna Waters Reserve, Apex Park (The Pines) and Lake Hume Tourist Park Beach. The lake is used for boating, fishing, kayaking, canoeing and paddleboarding, with public boat ramps at Apex Park, Bowna Waters Reserve, Kremur Street, Lake Hume Village and Mungabareena Reserve.
highlights: About 20km east of the Albury CBD
Boating, fishing, kayaking, canoeing and paddleboarding
Public boat ramps at five locations
Foreshore parks at Table Top Reserve, Bowna Waters, Apex Park and Lake Hume Tourist Park Beach

name: Eastern Hill Reserve
description: Eastern Hill sits east of the Albury CBD, where the ridgeline gives views of Lake Hume and the Kiewa Valley. The reserve connects to Mungabareena Reserve via the Hume and Hovell Walking Track and is used by bushwalkers, trail runners and mountain bikers. There are hiking and cycling trails, a self guided trail, picnic tables, seating and public toilets.
highlights: Free reserve with ridgeline views of Lake Hume and the Kiewa Valley
Linked to Mungabareena Reserve by the Hume and Hovell Walking Track
Hiking, trail running and mountain biking tracks
Self guided trail with picnic tables and seating

name: Murray River Canoe Hire
description: Operating since 1991, Murray River Canoe Hire rents two seater canoes and one and two seater sit on top kayaks for paddling the Murray River, and runs guided trips. Options range from a 1.5 hour short trip and a Thursday evening paddle through half day (17km) and full day (27km) hires to multi day trips covering 66km, plus dawn paddles and customised school group trips. Bookings are taken by phone or text.
highlights: Canoe and kayak hire on the Murray River since 1991
Half day 17km and full day 27km paddles
Thursday evening and dawn paddle trips

name: Jindera Pioneer Museum
description: A volunteer run pioneer museum on about two acres in Jindera, north of Albury, with more than 400 exhibits spread through preserved historic buildings including an 1874 blacksmith shop, a period store and dwellings, and machinery and transport displays. The collection focuses on the district's settler history and German heritage. Most visitors spend 60 to 90 minutes on site, and a Sunday tea room serves Devonshire teas and homemade baking.
highlights: More than 400 exhibits across two acres of preserved buildings
Displays on the district's German settler heritage
Sunday tea room with Devonshire teas
Open daily 10am to 4pm October to April and 10am to 3pm May to September
Adults $15, concession $10, children 5 to 12 $5, under 5 free

name: Bonegilla Migrant Experience
description: Block 19 at Bonegilla is the last surviving section of the post war migrant reception centre that received more than 300,000 new arrivals, and is now a heritage site open to the public. Visitors can walk through the original huts, follow the Suitcase Trail and see The Arc memorial sculpture, with guided tours available by appointment and education programs for schools. Entry is $8 for adults and $7 concession, children under 16 are free, and annual passes cost $14 and $12.
highlights: The last remaining block of the Bonegilla migrant reception centre
More than 300,000 post war migrants passed through the camp
Suitcase Trail and The Arc memorial sculpture
Open Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday, 10am to 4pm

name: Hyphen - Wodonga Library Gallery
description: Hyphen is Wodonga's library and gallery in the city's cultural precinct on Hovell Street. The gallery runs a rotating program of exhibitions by local and contemporary artists, while the library gives access to more than 3 million items through Libraries Victoria plus computers, free wi-fi, printing, storytime, book clubs and local history research help. The building is fully accessible with two lifts, and parking is off Havelock Street behind The Cube Wodonga.
highlights: Free entry gallery with rotating exhibitions
Library access to more than 3 million items via Libraries Victoria
Storytime, book clubs and local history research

name: Belvoir Park
description: Belvoir Park is a large open space in Wodonga with established trees and a lake full of water birds, and the gardens beside the lake are known locally as Sumsion Gardens. There are two playgrounds: a multi age area with elevated platforms, decks, slides, nets, a climbing wall, a liberty swing, swings, a sandpit and interactive panels; and an area for ages 6 to 14 with two flying foxes, a ninja warrior obstacle course, an all abilities carousel that fits two wheelchairs, a rope snake swing for six children, a four metre twisted slide and a 7.3 metre climbing tower. The park also has a walking track around the lake, an off leash dog park, a community woodfired oven, picnic and barbecue facilities, drinking fountains, shelters, seating and public toilets.
highlights: Free parkland with a lake and walking track
Two playgrounds including an all abilities carousel and liberty swing
Ninja warrior obstacle course and two flying foxes
Community woodfired oven, barbecues and public toilets

name: Huon Hill Regional Park
description: Huon Hill rises 263 metres above the Murray and Kiewa floodplains east of Wodonga, and its lookouts take in Lake Hume, the surrounding valleys and the twin cities. The 238 hectare regional park protects Box Gum Grassy Woodland across steep rolling hills and rocky outcrops. Four walking tracks total about 7.5km - the Summit Track (200m), Bundy Track (3km), Sheoak Track (2.5km) and Mistletoe Track (2km) - and facilities include lookouts, a directional cairn, electric barbecues, shelters, picnic tables, seating, composting toilets, information boards and car parking. Access is via Thomas Mitchell Drive to the Murray Valley Highway, then Whytes Road and Kenneth Watson Drive.
highlights: Free entry, lookouts over Lake Hume and Albury Wodonga
Summit Track is only 200m from the car park
Electric barbecues, shelters and picnic tables

name: 3D Lanes
description: 3D Lanes on Sanyo Drive, Wodonga has 14 tenpin bowling lanes, an 18 hole challenge mini golf course and an amusement arcade of prize winning redemption games, plus a licensed cafe serving food and drinks. It caters for birthday parties, family outings, corporate team events and casual walk in play. Open from 10am weekdays and 9am on weekends, closing late.
highlights: Birthday party and corporate group packages

name: Gateway Island Trail
description: A 4.3km sealed loop on Gateway Island, starting from Gateway Village behind The Lincoln on the Lincoln Causeway. The path follows the Murray River and Wodonga Creek through river red gums and eucalypts, and features sculptural works by local Aboriginal artists that reflect how First Nations people used the river's resources. Wildlife seen along the trail includes platypus, wallabies, water rats, wedge tailed eagles, kangaroos, bats and spoonbills.
highlights: Free 4.3km sealed loop suitable for walking and cycling
Sculptural works by local Aboriginal artists
Follows the Murray River and Wodonga Creek
Platypus, kangaroo and birdlife along the route
Starts at Gateway Village on the Lincoln Causeway

name: Wodonga WAVES
description: Wodonga WAVES is the city's summer outdoor swimming venue, with a 50 metre heated pool, a splash pad, a toddlers pool, a cafe and shaded areas. It is operated by Aligned Leisure as part of the Albury Wodonga Aquatics group of centres, and opening hours change with the season.

name: Army Museum Bandiana
description: The Army Museum Bandiana on Anderson Road holds what it describes as the largest military museum collection in Australia, with a particular focus on the history of the Australian Army's logistic corps. Displays cover Australia's military heritage across vehicles, equipment and personal collections. The museum is open Wednesday to Sunday, 9am to 3pm.
highlights: Described as the largest military museum collection in Australia
Focus on the Army's logistic corps history

name: High Country Rail Trail
description: An 81km rail trail running from Wodonga around Lake Hume to Tallangatta and up into the mountains at Shelley, passing Bandiana, Old Tallangatta, Bullioh, Darbyshire and Koetong. The surface is hot mix asphalt near Wodonga, chip seal in places and gravel beyond Old Tallangatta. The route crosses the 600 metre Sandy Creek Bridge and historic timber trestle bridges, is undulating to Bullioh and then climbs about 460 metres to Shelley.
highlights: 81km from Wodonga to Shelley via Tallangatta
Sealed near Wodonga, gravel in the upper sections
Crosses the 600 metre Sandy Creek Bridge
Passes the Old Tallangatta township site
Free to use, no permit required

name: Burke Museum and Beechworth Historic Precinct
description: The Beechworth Historic Precinct groups four gold era buildings in the centre of town: the Beechworth Courthouse, which houses the Kelly Trials Exhibition and its 270 degree wrap around multimedia experience; the Burke Museum, holding more than 30,000 items including Chinese, goldmining and natural history collections, objects linked to Robert O'Hara Burke and Dame Nellie Melba, and a recreated 19th century street of shops; the 1858 Telegraph Station, which once linked the town to the outside world by Morse code; and the Powder Magazine. Tickets and current opening information come through the Beechworth Visitor Information Centre on Ford Street.
highlights: Four gold era buildings in one precinct
Kelly Trials Exhibition in the Beechworth Courthouse
Burke Museum holds more than 30,000 items
1858 Telegraph Station and the Powder Magazine
Ticketing through the Beechworth Visitor Information Centre

name: Woolshed Falls
description: Woolshed Falls is a ten minute drive north of Beechworth in Chiltern-Mt Pilot National Park, where Reedy Creek spills across a broad sheet of granite. An observation deck gives views to the falls and the valley below, which is at its most dramatic after heavy rain, and self guided walking trails lead past alluvial gold workings from the days when thousands of diggers worked this ground. A 6km walking track links the falls back to Beechworth. The rocks are slippery, so sturdy footwear is advised and children should be supervised.
highlights: Free entry, in Chiltern-Mt Pilot National Park
Observation deck overlooking the falls and valley
Self guided walking trails past alluvial gold workings
Ten minute drive north of Beechworth
Rocks are slippery, sturdy footwear advised

name: Lake Sambell
description: Lake Sambell is a recreation reserve a short stroll from the centre of Beechworth, created in the 1920s out of the Rocky Mountain Mining Company's open cut sluice workings from the gold rush. There is a sandy beach swimming area with an adventure playground beside it, walking tracks through the reserve, two electric barbecues, picnic tables and seating. The Murray to the Mountains Rail Trail passes through the reserve.
highlights: Two electric barbecues and picnic tables
Murray to the Mountains Rail Trail passes through

name: Chiltern Athenaeum Museum
description: Built in 1866, the Chiltern Athenaeum on Conness Street is one of the region's most notable historic buildings and now holds a local history museum. The collection runs from goldfields era books and memorabilia to artworks and historic artefacts, with displays on notable locals including former Prime Minister Sir John McEwen and the author Henry Handel Richardson. It opens Wednesdays and Sundays from 10am to 3pm.
highlights: Goldfields era books, memorabilia and artefacts
Displays on Sir John McEwen and Henry Handel Richardson
In the heart of Chiltern's heritage streetscape

name: Chiltern-Mt Pilot National Park
description: This 21,636 hectare national park stretches between Beechworth and the low hills around Chiltern, protecting box ironbark country and a landscape shaped by gold mining. A short walk leads to the 545 metre Mount Pilot summit and a 360 degree view of the surrounding countryside, with Mount Buffalo visible on clear days. Yeddonba is an important Aboriginal site with original rock art, and the Mount Pilot area holds cultural significance for the Yorta Yorta Peoples. The 8.5km Whitebox Walking Track starts at the Honeyeater Picnic Area and takes two to three hours, and Woolshed Falls sits within the park. Prospecting is allowed with a Miner's Right.
highlights: Free entry, 21,636 hectares of box ironbark country
360 degree views from the 545 metre Mount Pilot summit
Yeddonba Aboriginal cultural site with rock art
8.5km Whitebox Walking Track from the Honeyeater Picnic Area
Woolshed Falls and Reedy Creek picnic area
Prospecting permitted with a Miner's Right

name: Karr's Reef Goldmine Tours
description: A fully guided gold history tour of Yackandandah run by local guide Greg. The tour starts by 4WD from where gold was first found along Commissioner's Creek, then finishes underground at the heritage protected Karr's Reef mine, worked from 1867 to 1884. Inside you can still see pick marks on the dirt walls and core holes from black powder blasting, walk the length of the quartz reef and see remaining gold in the rock. Tours run on demand and are booked by phone or email.
highlights: Guided 4WD and underground gold mine tour
Heritage protected mine worked from 1867 to 1884
Original pick marks and black powder blasting core holes

name: Yackandandah Gorge Scenic Walk
description: The gorge at Yackandandah was dug as a tail race to sluice gravel and sand for gold, first by hand and later deepened with dynamite, and the result is a twisting creek walk with cascades and shady overhanging trees. The signposted circuit is 3.5km and takes about 75 minutes, graded 2 on a hardened compacted surface with gentle hills and occasional steps, though the upper gorge is steeper and needs sure footing. A five minute access point from Bells Flat Road suits anyone who cannot manage the full walk. Gold panning is no longer permitted in the creek.
highlights: Grade 2 track on a hardened, compacted surface
Cascades and creek scenery through a gold era tail race
Short five minute access from Bells Flat Road
Information signs and car park at the trailhead

name: Wangaratta Art Gallery
description: Wangaratta Art Gallery sits in the city's arts and culture precinct on Ovens Street and shows a program of self curated and touring exhibitions covering contemporary and historic visual art, craft and design. The gallery has a particular focus on textiles and runs the biennial Wangaratta Contemporary Textile Award. Education programs, public talks and kids' art classes are scheduled alongside exhibitions. Entry is free and it opens Tuesday to Sunday, 10am to 4pm.
highlights: Self curated and touring exhibitions of art, craft and design
Kids' art classes and public talks

name: Murray to Mountains Rail Trail
description: One of Australia's best known rail trails, 137km of sealed path linking Wangaratta with Myrtleford, Bright, Beechworth and Yackandandah. It runs in four main sections: Wangaratta to Bright (82km) through the Ovens Valley, Everton to Yackandandah (38km) which climbs steeply through Beechworth, Wangaratta to Oxley (9km) in the King Valley, and Rutherglen to Wahgunyah (8km) across wine country. Most of the trail has gentle rail grades, with the steeper climbs on the Everton, Beechworth and Yackandandah sections.
highlights: 137km of sealed rail trail, free to use
Links Wangaratta, Beechworth, Yackandandah, Myrtleford and Bright
Flat 9km Wangaratta to Oxley section through the King Valley
8km Rutherglen to Wahgunyah spur across wine country
Steeper climbs between Everton, Beechworth and Yackandandah

name: Hotbake Albury
description: Bakery in the Albury CBD on Volt Lane, one of three Hotbake shops alongside Lavington and Wodonga. It opens at 6am on weekdays. There is also a wholesale side of the business, offering approved partners discounts of up to 40 per cent with in-store pick up or delivery seven days a week, plus special pricing on pies for fundraising pie drives.
highlights: Albury shop at 9 Volt Lane, open Mon-Fri 6am-4pm and Sat 7am-3pm
Approved wholesale partners receive discounts of up to 40 per cent
In-store pick up or delivery available seven days a week for wholesale orders
Special pricing on pies for fundraising pie drives
One of three Hotbake locations, with Lavington and Wodonga stores

name: Thurgoona Bakery
description: Family run bakery in Thurgoona Plaza that says it has been part of Thurgoona since the mid 1980s. It bakes bread in all varieties, rolls, cakes, pastries, pies, doughnuts, tortes and slices fresh on site daily and trades seven days from 6.30am. The bakery also caters for wholesale clients, sporting groups and special events.
highlights: Shopfront at 10 Schuter Avenue in Thurgoona Plaza
Open seven days from 6.30am, closed public holidays
Bakes bread, rolls, cakes, pastries, pies, doughnuts, tortes and slices
Describes itself as a family run business in Thurgoona since the mid 1980s
Caters for wholesale clients, sporting groups and special events

name: Full Cycle Albury
description: Bicycle sales and repair business based in Albury, run by a mechanic the site describes as having 28 years in the industry and a lifetime in the sport of cycling. Located at Cadell Place on Fitzmaurice Street

name: The Perennial
description: The Perennial is a modern Australian cafe on Lake Albert Road at Kooringal serving brunch dishes such as bacon and egg rolls, hotcakes, corn fritters and eggs benedict. It pours ST. ALi coffee, using the Orthodox blend for all in-house espresso, delivered weekly from Melbourne. The cafe is closed Sundays and public holidays.
highlights: Bacon and egg rolls, hotcakes and corn fritters
Kooringal shopfront on Lake Albert Road

name: The Brew
description: The Brew is a coffee shop and eatery on Coleman Street that aims to bring people together over coffee and food in a spacious, relaxed setting. It supports local products and produce and encourages sustainable living. Reservations and online ordering are available through its website.

name: Infuso
description: Infuso is a cafe in the Turvey Tops Shopping Centre, minutes from the Wagga Wagga CBD, serving all-day breakfast, lunch and coffee with takeaway available. It uses award-winning BeanRoasters coffee beans. The business also runs a mobile food and drink van that can be hired for conferences, weddings, corporate and sporting events.
addressLine: Shop 3a, Turvey Tops Shopping Centre, 44-66 Fernleigh Road

name: The Gardens Wagga
description: The Gardens Wagga is a cafe and function centre inside the Wagga Wagga Botanic Gardens. The cafe serves coffee, brunch and lunch surrounded by the gardens, and the venue also hosts weddings, milestone birthdays, corporate events and school formals. An online store sells platters, grazing boxes and corporate catering.
addressLine: Wagga Wagga Botanic Gardens, 43 Tom Wood Drive
highlights: Cafe inside the Wagga Wagga Botanic Gardens
Platters and grazing boxes to order

name: The Fast Lane Drive-Thru Coffee Wagga
description: The Fast Lane Drive-Thru Coffee on Hammond Avenue is a drive-through cafe aimed at commuters, serving coffee plus on-the-go breakfast, lunch and travel snacks. The business roasts its own signature coffee blend and sources food and drinks from local suppliers where it can.

name: Artisan Baker - So French, So Fresh
description: Artisan Baker is a French-owned and operated boulangerie and patisserie on Morgan Street with cafe seating and barista coffee. It specialises in sourdough and French-style breads, with patisserie items including opera cake, mille feuille and frangipane tarts. In-house pies, sausage rolls and a soup of the day are also available.
highlights: Opera cake, mille feuille and frangipane tarts

name: Mock Orange
description: Mock Orange is a cafe in the Lake Village shops on Gregory Crescent at Lake Albert. It has outdoor seating.
highlights: Cafe at the Lake Village shops

name: Lake Village Bakery
description: Lake Village Bakery is a bakery and cafe in the Lake Village shops on Gregory Crescent at Lake Albert. It offers takeaway and has outdoor seating.

name: Lake Village Takeaway
description: Lake Village Takeaway is a takeaway food shop in the Lake Village shops on Gregory Crescent at Lake Albert. It trades alongside the Lake Village Bakery and the Mock Orange cafe in the same block.

name: Cafe Phoenix
description: Cafe Phoenix is a cafe on Hammond Avenue in East Wagga Wagga. It has outdoor seating.

name: Table and Graze
description: Table and Graze is a family-run Wagga Wagga catering business established in 2017 that builds grazing tables, grazing boxes, platters and breakfast boxes for weddings, parties, corporate events and festivals. It covers much of the Riverina and also travels interstate for larger events. The business sources from local suppliers including Wollundry Grove Olives, Junee Licorice and Chocolate Factory, Riverina Grove and Three Hives Beekeeping.
highlights: Covers Wagga Wagga and much of the Riverina

name: Quinty Bakehouse
description: Quinty Bakehouse in Uranquinty bakes sourdough, cobbs and baguettes along with handcrafted tarts, cookies and cakes. It also serves cooked breakfast, a wide lunch selection and barista coffee with latte art. High tea is available at the Uranquinty store by booking, and the bakehouse runs school holiday classes for children.

name: The Ten Mile
description: The Ten Mile is a licensed eatery in central Holbrook run by regional chef Sarah King, set inside a 100-year-old building that once operated as the local garage and mechanic's workshop. The kitchen works with farm gate produce including Holbrook Paddock Eggs, Bicycle Baker breads from Albury and Mansfield Coffee Merchants, with local wines from Borambola and Fowles and craft beer from Bridge Road Brewers. A retail store on site stocks cookbooks, food items and kitchenware, and group bookings and functions can be catered.
highlights: Farm gate produce and local wines
Retail store with cookbooks and kitchenware

name: Victoria Hotel
description: A Baylis Street pub in the Wagga CBD with a bistro serving pub classics and grilled meats for lunch and dinner. The venue shows live sport, runs gaming and TAB facilities, and puts on live music, DJs and karaoke nights. Functions and events can be booked, and the hotel runs the Harvest Gold membership program.
highlights: On Baylis Street in the CBD
Bistro lunch and dinner seven days

name: William Farrer Hotel
description: A CBD pub and bistro on Peter Street, known locally as The Faz. The bistro serves lunch and dinner using locally sourced produce and grilled dishes, and there is a beer garden plus accommodation upstairs. The hotel shows live sport and hosts functions and regular promotions.
highlights: CBD pub known as The Faz

name: Riverina Hotel
description: A heritage Fitzmaurice Street pub, known as The Riv, that has been trading since 1851. It runs a family friendly bistro with pub classics, chef's specials and a kids menu, plus a drive-thru bottle shop. Live sport plays on big screens, there are TAB facilities, Thursday steak night and Wednesday trivia.
highlights: Family friendly bistro with kids meals
Live sport on big screens and TAB

name: The Astor Hotel & Bar
description: Accommodation, restaurant and bar on Edward Street near the CBD and the railway station. The Mallee Grill restaurant serves steaks and pub classics Monday to Saturday evenings, with pizzas available in the bar and restaurant from 10am daily and lunch on Friday and Saturday. There is a happy hour Thursday to Saturday and function facilities for conferences and private events.
highlights: Boutique rooms near the CBD and railway station
43 rooms near the CBD and railway station

name: Sportsmens Club Hotel
description: A Kincaid Street pub near the Murrumbidgee Turf Club racecourse, known locally as the Sporties. It has a spacious beer garden, a bistro with alfresco seating, weekday lunch specials and nightly dinner specials. Six refurbished pub-style rooms are available upstairs and the venue takes function bookings.
highlights: Weekday lunch and nightly dinner specials

name: Jungle Duke Hotel
description: A family owned hotel on Fitzmaurice Street overlooking the Murrumbidgee River, open seven days for lunch and dinner from 11.30am. The renovated venue serves cocktails including margaritas alongside dishes such as ginger beer battered fish and chips and schnitzel, with lunch specials on the board. There is outdoor seating and the hotel is wheelchair accessible.
highlights: Family owned, overlooking the Murrumbidgee River
Open seven days for lunch and dinner

name: Bar Olivette
description: A basement speakeasy-style bar on Fitzmaurice Street built around a 1920s prohibition theme. It pours prohibition-style cocktails and keeps an extensive whiskey and spirits collection including rare blends sourced from overseas, alongside bar food. Walk-ins are welcome but reservations are preferred, and the bar runs occasional Sunday Smuggler's Compass events.
highlights: Extensive whiskey and rare spirits selection

name: Tilly's Wagga
description: A restaurant and cocktail bar on Baylis Street serving share plates and main meals alongside an extensive cocktail list of seasonal signatures and classics. The venue has a rooftop deck and several function spaces including the Parlour Room, and runs karaoke and DJ nights. A nightclub operates on Saturday nights from 10pm.
highlights: Restaurant and cocktail bar on Baylis Street
Function spaces including the Parlour Room

name: Thirsty Crow Brewing Co
description: A family owned, independent brewpub on Fitzmaurice Street with the working brewery visible from the front bar. It pours its own beers including stouts, rice lagers and ales, plus cider and regional wines, and the kitchen sends out tacos, nachos, salads, pizzas and burgers. There is outdoor seating, function space and live music on weekends.
highlights: Working microbrewery visible from the front bar
House-brewed stouts, rice lagers and ales
Kitchen serving tacos, nachos, pizzas and burgers

name: Wagga RSL Club
description: A licensed RSL club on the corner of Kincaid and Dobbs Streets in the Wagga CBD, open from 10am to 3am every day and closed only on Christmas Day. Breakfast is served from 8am daily, and the club runs dining venues, bars, a sports bar, gaming and weekly raffles. It hosts entertainment, kids dining and functions, and members get access to club deals and social events. The club also runs the Wagga RSL Bowling Club, which has two championship greens and offers barefoot bowls bookings.
addressLine: Corner of Kincaid Street and Dobbs Street
highlights: Open 10am to 3am every day, closed Christmas Day
Two championship bowling greens and barefoot bowls

name: Farmers Home Hotel
description: A Hammond Avenue pub just over the bridge from the Wagga CBD, with an outdoor beer garden and a bistro serving lunch and dinner seven days. The venue is family friendly, has on-site parking and takes function bookings. Trading runs to 3am Monday to Saturday.
highlights: Bistro lunch and dinner seven days

name: Palm & Pawn Motor Inn & Tavern
description: A tavern and motor inn on Hampden Avenue at North Wagga, established in 1976. It has an extensive beer garden with a children's playground and a bistro serving lunch and dinner daily, with steaks, burgers and weeknight specials. A courtesy bus runs Wednesday to Sunday nights and the venue hosts functions and events.
highlights: Extensive beer garden with kids playground
Courtesy bus Wednesday to Sunday nights

name: Black Swan Hotel
description: A small country pub on Gardiner Street at North Wagga Wagga, listed as trading daily from 10am to midnight. It serves cold beer and spirits along with bar and light meals, and the venue is used for functions and receptions.
highlights: Country pub at North Wagga Wagga

name: Tolland Hotel
description: A family friendly local hotel at Tolland, about 4km from the Wagga CBD. It runs a family bistro with a kids menu and indoor play area, a TAB and sports bar with large projector screens, and an outside deck. There is live music on Friday nights, plus function facilities with a courtesy bus and food and beverage packages.
highlights: Family bistro with kids menu and indoor play area
TAB and sports bar with projector screens

name: Kooringal Hotel
description: A suburban hotel on Fay Avenue that has been trading since 1967 under the line "your local since 1967". Facilities include a bar, bistro open daily for lunch and dinner, TAB, a VIP lounge, multiple beer gardens and a children's playground. The venue caters for functions from casual gatherings to formal events and runs a loyalty membership program.
highlights: Bistro open daily for lunch and dinner

name: Turvey Park Hotel
description: A renovated local pub on Bolger Avenue with a courtyard, dining room and betting lounge. The bistro serves lunch and dinner daily with weekday lunch specials and nightly dinner deals, and there is a drive-through bottle shop. Live music plays on weekends and the venue takes function bookings.
highlights: Courtyard, dining room and betting lounge
Weekday lunch specials and nightly dinner deals

name: Ashmont Inn Hotel
description: A recently renovated, family friendly hotel on Tobruk Street in Ashmont, close to the Pomingalarna bicycle park. It serves food and drinks and has an attached bottle shop. Trading is 10am to midnight Monday to Saturday and 10am to 10pm Sunday.

name: Rules Club Wagga
description: A large licensed club on Fernleigh Road with a bistro serving wood-fired pizzas, a cafe, a sports bar, a gaming room and multiple function rooms including a boardroom and bridal room. Outside there are bowling greens with barefoot bowls, a sports oval, netball courts and tennis courts. A courtesy bus runs, the club holds bingo and raffles, and the adjoining 79-room Quality Hotel provides accommodation with secure parking.
highlights: Bistro with wood-fired pizzas and a cafe
Sports oval, netball and tennis courts

name: The Blamey Hotel
description: A family friendly pub and bistro on Main Street at Lake Albert with a free courtesy bus. The bistro serves lunch and dinner daily, sport plays on large screens, and there is a bottle shop with a delivery service. Live entertainment runs Friday and Saturday evenings, and the venue has gaming and TAB plus function space.

name: Uranquinty Hotel
description: A village pub on Morgan Street at Uranquinty, open Monday to Sunday from midday. It has a public bar with TAB and gaming machines, a bottle shop with takeaway, and bistro meals for dine-in or takeaway Wednesday to Sunday. The pub runs a courtesy bus, offers free camping and a children's play area, and displays historical memorabilia, with regular raffles and pub draws through the week.
highlights: Public bar with TAB and gaming machines
Bistro meals Wednesday to Sunday, dine-in or takeaway

name: Junee Hotel
description: A heritage country hotel on Seignior Street, trading since 1878 when it opened as the Railway Hotel, with Federation Filigree and Art Nouveau detailing. The kitchen serves lunch from midday and dinner from 6pm using Riverina produce, and there is a bar, beer garden and bottle shop. Heritage guest rooms are available upstairs, dogs are welcome in the outdoor areas, and the hotel takes function bookings.
highlights: Operating since 1878, originally the Railway Hotel
Federation Filigree and Art Nouveau building
Lunch and dinner using Riverina produce

name: Criterion Hotel Gundagai
description: A Sheridan Street pub in Gundagai whose bar carries original oil-painted murals depicting bushrangers and the 1852 flood. Meals and pizzas are served seven nights a week in a family friendly setting. The hotel has King Single, Queen and Family accommodation rooms, and runs live music, happy hour, pool competitions and sport on screen.
highlights: Bar with original oil-painted historical murals
King Single, Queen and Family rooms

name: Narrandera Ex-Servicemen's Club
description: A licensed club on Bolton Street in Narrandera describing itself as a venue for dining, entertainment and community. The Riverina Wok N Grill restaurant operates on site alongside the bar. The club runs weekly raffles, member badge draws, live entertainment, social dancing classes, trivia, bingo and poker, and takes function bookings.
highlights: Riverina Wok N Grill restaurant on site
Weekly raffles and member badge draws

name: Coolamon Hotel
description: A historic pub on Cowabbie Street in Coolamon, established in 1880, split into several distinct spaces: The Garden outdoor bar, The Dining Room, The Front Bar for cocktails and casual drinks, The Glasshouse covered dining area, The Lounge and The Long Room for functions. The pub is open daily from 11.30am with the kitchen running 11.30am to 2.30pm and 5.30pm to 8.30pm, and pizza available seven days. Accommodation, weddings, functions and online ordering are all offered.
highlights: The Long Room for functions and weddings

name: The Rock Memorial Bowling Club
description: A lawn bowls club on Urana Street at The Rock that has been operating since 1939. Dining is at Crystal's Restaurant with an Australian menu, and there is a bar alongside the greens. The club programs live music, bingo and trivia nights, and offers membership with discounts and access to club events.

name: Culcairn Hotel
description: A country hotel on Railway Parade in Culcairn offering budget accommodation in Queen, Single, Twin Share and Family rooms, all with shared bathrooms upstairs and flat-screen smart TVs. The venue also runs a bistro, a beer garden and a playground. Extended stay discounts are available and accommodation reception is closed on Christmas Day.
highlights: Budget pub accommodation with shared bathrooms
Queen, Single, Twin Share and Family rooms

name: Holbrook Returned Servicemen's Club
description: A returned servicemen's club on Swift Street in Holbrook with a restaurant, bar, and Keno and TAB betting. The club takes in a golf club and a bowls club, along with boating and angling sections. It offers memberships and hosts functions, trading 10am to 9pm Saturday to Thursday and until 10.30pm on Friday.

name: Bush & Campbell
description: Accounting and advisory firm at 30 Blake Street in central Wagga Wagga. The practice lists taxation and accounting, business advisory services, succession planning, CFO services, financial planning, audit and assurance, and self managed superannuation. Alongside the Wagga Wagga office the firm also has offices at Lockhart, Tumbarumba and Tumut.
highlights: Taxation and accounting for individuals and businesses
Also has Lockhart, Tumbarumba and Tumut offices

name: WDF Accounting + Advisory
description: Accounting and advisory practice at 135-137 Peter Street, Wagga Wagga. Service lines listed on their site are tax and compliance, business advisory, superannuation, smart accounting, bookkeeping and payroll, and an HR partner service. The office is open weekdays from 8:30am to 5:00pm.
highlights: Tax and compliance work for businesses and individuals

name: Farrell Lusher Solicitors
description: Law firm at 39 Fitzmaurice Street that has practised in Wagga Wagga since 1910. Areas of work listed are family law including divorce, property settlements and parenting orders, criminal and driving matters, wills and estates, conveyancing, personal injury litigation and commercial law. Reception is open Monday to Friday from 9am to 5pm.
highlights: Family law, divorce and parenting matters
Criminal law, AVOs and driving offences
Wills, probate and powers of attorney

name: Tankard's Law
description: Criminal and traffic law practice in Shop 6 at 54 Fitzmaurice Street, Wagga Wagga. The firm's listed work covers drug offences, assaults, break and enter, fraud and firearms matters on the criminal side, and drink driving, drug driving, speeding, dangerous driving, licence appeals and heavy vehicle offences on the traffic side.
highlights: Fitzmaurice Street office in the CBD

name: Bower Wood Lawyers
description: Law firm at 57 Gurwood Street, Wagga Wagga, with a second office at 54 The Parade, Tumbarumba. The practice works in business and commercial law, conveyancing and property development, and estate planning and administration.

name: Fitzpatricks Real Estate
description: Real estate agency on Baylis Street in the Wagga Wagga CBD. The agency handles residential sales and rentals, commercial property, property management, rural property and land sales, and offers free property appraisals along with maintenance request and e-alert services for owners and tenants.
highlights: Property management with online maintenance requests

name: Kitson Property
description: Wagga Wagga real estate agency at 66 Baylis Street handling sales, leasing and property management. The agency provides sales appraisals, investment advice, tenant forms and an online maintenance request system for renters.

name: Ray White Wagga Wagga
description: Real estate office at 83 Morgan Street covering residential, land, commercial and rural sales plus rentals and property management. The office states it has been part of the Wagga real estate industry for over 30 years and also operates offices at Junee and Coolamon. Free in-person and desktop appraisals are offered.
highlights: Also operates Junee and Coolamon offices

name: Paper Plane Finance
description: Mortgage broking business listed on Baylis Street, Wagga Wagga. The broker works across home loans, investment loans and refinancing, assisting first home buyers, repeat purchasers and property investors.

name: Angry Ant Web Design
description: Web and design studio with offices in Wagga Wagga and the Shoalhaven. Services listed are web design, branding, graphic design and social media, with client work described across government, tourism, medical, hospitality, festival and agricultural sectors.
highlights: Offices in Wagga Wagga and the Shoalhaven

name: Quickprint Wagga
description: Printing business on Fitzmaurice Street covering business stationery, promotional items, design, event and wedding printing, signage and labels. The shop trades weekdays from 8:30am to 4:30pm and is closed on weekends.

name: Khan Signs
description: Locally owned signage business on Pearson Street that describes servicing Wagga and Australia for over 30 years. Work covers vehicle signage and wraps, fleet branding, illuminated and 3D lettering, shopfront and reception signage, safety and wayfinding signs, large format and digital printing, laser cutting and engraving, and paint protection film. The business is a 3M Select partner.

name: Best St. Dental
description: Dental practice at 122 Best Street offering family and preventive dentistry, cosmetic and smile design work, orthodontics, dental implants, root canal treatment, periodontal treatment and hygiene, teeth whitening, sleep apnoea and snoring treatment, and emergency appointments. The practice offers CEREC same-day crowns and is open weekdays from 8am to 5pm.
highlights: Dental implants and root canal treatment

name: Shumack Dental & Implants
description: Dental practice on Trail Street covering family dentistry, restorative work such as fillings, crowns, bridges, dentures and veneers, and single and full arch dental implants. The practice also lists periodontics, sleep dentistry, orthodontics, mouthguards, a mobile dentistry service and same-day emergency appointments. It opens weekdays 8am to 5pm and every second Saturday morning.
highlights: Single and full arch dental implants

name: Wagga Physiotherapy and Sports Injury Centre
description: Physiotherapy and sports injury rehabilitation practice at 45 Best Street. The centre states it has been operating for over 30 years and works alongside general practitioners, specialists, gyms and local sporting groups.
highlights: Works with GPs, specialists and sporting clubs

name: Granger Chiropractic
description: Chiropractic clinic at 67 Johnston Street treating neck pain and headaches, arthritis and sports injuries, with care for families and children. Techniques listed include the Activator Method, Diversified Technique, Sacral Occipital Technique and the Thompson Technique. The practice is a member of the Australian Chiropractors Association.
highlights: Activator, Diversified, SOT and Thompson techniques

name: Lightfoot Podiatry
description: Locally owned podiatry clinic in the D'Hudson Arcade on Baylis Street. Treatments listed are general toenail care, corns and calluses, ingrown toenail removal using the BS Brace, advice on tinea and other foot infections, and diabetic foot assessments and complications. The clinic is on the ground floor for disability access and is Department of Veterans Affairs approved. It consults Tuesdays and Wednesdays, 9am to 4pm.
addressLine: Shop 6, Ground Floor, D'Hudson Arcade, 176-178 Baylis Street
highlights: General toenail, corn and callus care
Ingrown toenail treatment with BS Brace
Ground floor arcade location with disability access

name: Zacharia Naumann Optometry
description: Independent optometry practice at 210 Baylis Street. Services include comprehensive eye examinations, children's vision assessments, myopia control and orthokeratology, dry eye treatment, computer vision care and emergency eye care. The dispensary carries frames, sunglasses, contact lenses, sports eyewear, safety specs and Rodenstock DNEye biometric lenses. Late consultations run on Thursdays and the practice opens Saturday mornings.
highlights: Frames, contact lenses, sports and safety eyewear

name: Lake Road Veterinary Hospital
description: Veterinary hospital on Lake Albert Road that states it is open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. Services listed include consultations, diagnostics, advanced medical care, rehabilitation, grooming, puppy preschool, wildlife care and referral support for other veterinary practices.
highlights: Open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year

name: Kooringal Vet Hospital
description: Veterinary hospital at 2 Kimberley Drive, Tatton. Healthcare services include vaccinations, health checks, microchipping, radiography, ultrasonography and parasite control, while surgical work covers dental, desexing, ophthalmology, orthopaedic, soft tissue and emergency procedures. The clinic also offers behavioural advice, grooming, nutrition guidance, puppy preschool and rabbit and reptile care, and lists a 24 hour emergency service.
highlights: Dental, orthopaedic and soft tissue surgery

name: Michael O'Reilly Pharmacy
description: Pharmacy at 67 Baylis Street in the Wagga Wagga CBD. Services listed are PBS, concession and DVA dispensing, vaccinations including flu, whooping cough, MMR and COVID-19, sleep apnoea consultations and equipment, weekly medicines packs, MedsChecks, blood pressure and blood glucose monitoring, bowel cancer screening, baby weighing and absence from work certificates. Scripts can be uploaded online and appointments booked through the site.

name: Southcity Community Pharmacy
description: Pharmacy in the South City Shopping Centre on Tanda Place. The pharmacy offers Webster packing, custom compounding, online prescriptions and delivery, vaccinations, sleep apnoea support, pharmacist consultations and Farm Door frozen meals. It trades seven days, 8am to 7pm on weekdays and 9am to 5pm on weekends.
addressLine: Shop 5A, South City Shopping Centre, 1-7 Tanda Place

name: Lulu & Kit Haircutters
description: Fitzmaurice Street salon doing men's and women's cutting, colour work including highlights, foils, balayage, freehand placement, colour correction and toning, plus blow drying, curls, straightening and wedding and event styling. Treatments include O&M and Christophe Robin ranges, and the salon stocks Kevin Murphy, Eleven, O&M, GHD, Cloud Nine, Redken and K18. Late night trading on Thursdays.
highlights: Stocks Kevin Murphy, Eleven, O&M and K18

name: Big Barber Delux
description: Barber shop in Sturt Mall on Baylis Street, one of two Big Barber Delux shops in Wagga Wagga alongside the Marketplace store. The barbers do men's, seniors' and boys' haircuts, beard trims and styling, wet shaves and hair tattoos, and sell hair and beard care products. No appointment is needed and walk-ins are welcome.

name: BY KIRRA Skin & Beauty
description: Skin and beauty studio at 105 Forsyth Street offering facials aimed at hydration, brightening and ageing concerns, waxing and tinting, tanning, and professional makeup for special occasions, photoshoots and corporate events. Bridal makeup and gift vouchers are available, and the studio retails Medik8, iS Clinical, Vida Glow and ISSADA skincare. Appointments run Tuesday to Saturday.
highlights: Stocks Medik8, iS Clinical, Vida Glow and ISSADA
Open Tuesday to Saturday by appointment

name: Conspiracy Tattoo
description: Tattoo studio at 27 Baylis Street doing custom designs as well as pre-existing artwork. The studio describes medical grade hygiene using single-use needles and autoclave sterilisation, and is a member of the Australian Tattooists Guild.
highlights: Member of the Australian Tattooists Guild

name: Possums Early Learning Centre
description: Long day care centre at 7 Forsyth Street for children from six weeks to five years, running two rooms, Little Possums and the Preschool Room. The centre operates 8am to 6pm Monday to Friday, 52 weeks a year excluding public holidays, and families can access the Child Care Subsidy.
highlights: Long day care from six weeks to five years

name: CBM Meats
description: Wholesale and retail butcher located at the rear of 61 Baylis Street, Wagga Wagga. The shop sells premium cuts, smallgoods and smoked meats, with a range built around Riverina Angus beef, Australian pork and Riverina lamb. It trades weekdays 9am to 6pm and weekends 9am to 3pm.
highlights: Riverina Angus beef and Riverina lamb
Behind the Victoria Hotel on Baylis Street

name: Little Triffids Flowers
description: Florist and gift shop at 30 Fitzmaurice Street selling bouquets, potted plants and a gift range that takes in jewellery, baby items, beauty products, books, stationery, food and drink, garden wares and homewares. The shop does wedding and funeral flowers and runs workshops. Open Monday 9am to 2pm, Tuesday to Friday 9am to 5pm and Saturday 9am to 2pm.

name: Kidsons Cycles
description: Bike shop at 105 Fitzmaurice Street stocking road and mountain bikes from Merida, Cervelo, Specialized, Trek and Cannondale, BMX from DK, Fit Bike Co, GT and Kink, and kids bikes. The workshop offers repairs and a range of service packages from a deluxe bike wash to roadworthy, general, premium and platinum services, plus bike fitting sessions of about an hour. New bikes come with a free first service.
highlights: Road, mountain, BMX and kids bikes
Merida, Cervelo, Specialized, Trek and Cannondale
Free first service with a new bike

name: Gateway Bookshop
description: Independent bookshop in The Piazza on Baylis Street. The range covers children's and adult fiction, non-fiction, educational resources across several levels, special edition books and teacher diaries, and the shop also runs VR escape room experiences. Open Tuesday to Friday 10am to 5pm and Saturday 10am to 1pm.

name: Diamonds on Baylis Jewellers
description: Jewellery shop at 80 Baylis Street that has traded since 1984 and handcrafts rings, chains, pendants, earrings and bracelets in 9ct and 18ct yellow, white and rose gold. Stones used include diamonds, peridot, aquamarine, morganite, ruby and topaz, and the shop carries Adina and Citizen watches. On-site services cover custom design, repairs and restoration, ring resizing, stone resetting and appraisals.
highlights: On-site repairs, resizing and stone resetting

name: Allison Music Wagga
description: Locally owned music shop at 85 Forsyth Street that says it has served Wagga Wagga and the Riverina for over 23 years. Stock covers acoustic, electric, classical and bass guitars, amplifiers, acoustic and digital drums, acoustic and digital pianos, keyboards, folk instruments such as banjo, mandolin, ukulele and harmonica, orchestral instruments, PA and recording gear, sheet music and apparel.

name: Riverina Driving Academy
description: Driving school teaching learner drivers across Wagga Wagga and district, including Ashmont, Bourkelands, Estella, Forest Hill, Glenfield Park, Gumly Gumly, Kooringal, Lake Albert, Lloyd, Mount Austin, Tatton, Tolland and Turvey Park. Lessons run 60 minutes in dual-control automatic Honda Jazz cars, with a package of five lessons plus a sixth at half price. The instructor is Keys2Drive accredited.
highlights: Five lesson package with sixth at half price
Covers Wagga suburbs and nearby villages
Pick-up across Wagga Wagga and district

name: Rapley's Nursery and Landscape Supplies
description: Nursery and landscape supply yard at 56 Cummins Road, Lake Albert. The business sells locally grown plants and advanced trees alongside soils, mulches and landscape products, and offers planting advice, planning and design assistance, soil testing and delivery through Wagga Wagga and surrounding areas. Open weekdays 8am to 5pm and weekends 8:30am to 3pm.
highlights: Locally grown plants and advanced trees

name: Storehouse Botanica
description: Florist and gift store at 1 Humphrys Street, Junee. Arrangements are offered in pastel, tonal, bright and wildflower styles, and the shop also carries home fragrance, bath and body products, books, clothing and accessories. Next business day delivery is available in Junee and surrounding areas.
highlights: Home fragrance, bath and body gifts
Next business day delivery in Junee and district

name: Monty & Moo
description: Clothing, gifts and homewares store on Albury Street, Holbrook. The range covers dresses, shirts, knitwear and jackets, accessories including belts, jewellery, handbags and footwear, plus home and garden goods, bath and beauty products, greeting cards and stationery.

name: Skinner & Associates
description: Law firm founded in 1969 with an office at 24 Balfour Street, Culcairn and a second office in Albury. Practice areas listed are commercial and corporate law, conveyancing and property law, family law, wills and estates, dispute resolution and litigation, employment law, public notary work and court and tribunal appearances.
highlights: Family law and wills and estates

name: Custom Music
description: Music store on East Street, Narrandera, one of three Custom Music stores along with Griffith and Wagga Wagga. Stock includes guitars, ukuleles, amplifiers, drums, pianos, brass and wind instruments, violins and home recording equipment, and the business sells, installs and services PA systems and lighting for schools, clubs and churches. The Narrandera store opens weekdays 10am to 5pm and Saturday 9am to noon.
highlights: Guitars, drums, pianos and orchestral instruments
Installation and service for schools, clubs and churches
Stores at Narrandera, Griffith and Wagga Wagga

name: International Hotel Wagga Wagga
description: A hotel on the corner of the Sturt Highway and Lake Albert Road with 81 hotel rooms and suites, minutes from the Wagga Wagga CBD. Free Wi-Fi is provided and room service comes from Pinnacle's Restaurant and Bar, where the executive chef builds seasonal menus around regional produce. Apartment accommodation is also offered at the Mill Residence.
addressLine: Corner Sturt Highway and Lake Albert Road
highlights: Pinnacle's Restaurant and Bar on site
Wheelchair access and disability awareness trained staff

name: Mercure Wagga Wagga
description: A central Morgan Street hotel with 86 rooms made up of hotel rooms and self-contained serviced apartments, the apartments taking up to nine guests. Rooms have flat-screen TVs with free Foxtel, free Wi-Fi, in-room safes and tea and coffee facilities. There is a swimming pool, free on-site parking, four meeting rooms and the One Morgan Street restaurant and bar, plus free pool passes to the Oasis Aquatic Centre across the road.
highlights: One Morgan Street restaurant and bar
Four meeting rooms for events and weddings
Free pool passes to Oasis Aquatic Centre

name: Mantra Pavilion Hotel Wagga Wagga
description: A Kincaid Street hotel built around a 109-foot fabric roof, the largest of its kind in the world. Rooms include marble bathrooms, spas, mini-bars and balcony access. The hotel provides free Wi-Fi throughout, an arrival and departure lounge, tour desk, conference and meeting facilities, on-site parking and guest laundry, and sits alongside the city's restaurants, cafes, microbrewery and shopping.
highlights: Rooms with marble bathrooms and spas

name: Townhouse Hotel Wagga
description: A Morgan Street hotel in downtown Wagga Wagga with several room types and separate apartments. Guests get free use of the indoor heated aquatic centre and gym directly across the road, plus free wireless internet throughout. The Oakroom Restaurant and Bar serves guests in the restaurant or by room service.
highlights: Oakroom Restaurant and Bar on site
Free entry to the aquatic centre and gym across the road
Apartments as well as hotel rooms

name: St Hugh Hotel
description: A Forsyth Street hotel in central Wagga Wagga with four room categories: St Hugh Signature, Family, Accessible and Luxury. Rooms have custom king beds, smart TVs and secured Wi-Fi, and guest services run seven days a week. The hotel lists wheelchair access, accessible bathrooms and parking, hearing loop systems and staff trained in disability awareness.
highlights: Signature, Family, Accessible and Luxury rooms
Custom king beds and smart TVs

name: The Charles Boutique Hotel & Dining
description: A boutique hotel on Tarcutta Street with boutique king rooms, hotel rooms, suites and self-contained apartments finished in modern interiors. The Charles Dining Room serves dinner Tuesday to Saturday from 5:30pm and breakfast Tuesday to Friday from 6:45am, with tasting menus and a la carte built on Riverina ingredients. Vegan and gluten free options are catered for.
highlights: Boutique king rooms, suites and self-contained apartments
The Charles Dining Room open Tuesday to Saturday for dinner
Tasting menu and a la carte using Riverina produce

name: Quality Hotel Rules Club Wagga
description: A hotel of 79 units, four of them accessible, connected directly to the Rules Club precinct on Fernleigh Road. Rooms are soundproofed and air conditioned with 137cm smart TVs, free Wi-Fi or Ethernet and complimentary tea, coffee and biscuits. There is secure card-access parking, an electric vehicle charging station, conference and board rooms, fitness centre access and pushbikes for guests, with the club's cafe, restaurant and sports bar next door.
highlights: Directly connected to the Rules Club
Guest pushbikes and fitness centre access

name: Wagga RSL Motel & Apartments
description: Motel accommodation within the Wagga RSL Club on Kincaid Street. Room types run from Executive Suite and Easy Access Suite through Executive, Deluxe, Corner and Luxury Spa Suites, plus four self-contained two-bedroom apartments sleeping up to five. There is a solar heated pool, and guests have direct access to the club's dining venues, bars and live entertainment. The city centre is about a ten minute walk.
highlights: Executive, Deluxe, Corner and Luxury Spa Suites
Club dining, bars and entertainment on site
About ten minutes walk to the city centre

name: Boulevarde Motor Inn
description: An Edward Street motor inn where all rooms are ground floor, air conditioned and fully furnished, with 55 inch 4K Samsung TVs carrying Foxtel and free Netflix. The property has gardens, a barbecue area, an outdoor swimming pool and a guest laundry, and family rooms are available. It sits near the CBD and both the Wagga Wagga Rural Referral and Calvary hospitals.
highlights: All rooms on the ground floor
Foxtel and free Netflix in rooms

name: Best Western Ambassador Motor Inn & Apartments
description: A motor inn on Edward Street with Queen Rooms, Deluxe Twin, Accessible Twin, Family Suite, Signature Spa Suite and Two Bedroom Villa accommodation. Rooms carry 43 inch smart TVs, free wireless internet, electric blankets and work desks, with a kitchenette or full kitchen depending on the type. The property has an outdoor saltwater pool open October to April, a barbecue and garden area, free on-site parking and a self-service guest laundry, with continental breakfast seven days.
highlights: Rooms, family suites, spa suite and two bedroom villas
Outdoor saltwater pool October to April

name: Club Motel and Apartments
description: A Morgan Street motel with accommodation ranging from economy single rooms to larger deluxe rooms with small kitchens and two-bedroom family units. Free secure parking, Wi-Fi and 24 hour service are provided and late check-ins are accepted. There is a steakhouse and bar on site, with a pool and gym across the road and the main street shops and restaurants nearby.
highlights: Economy singles through to two-bedroom family units
Pool and gym across the road

name: Seven Inn
description: A 26-room motor inn on the Sturt Highway at Gumly Gumly, just east of Wagga Wagga. Rooms have reverse cycle air conditioning, a 40 inch smart television, work desk, open wardrobe, blackout curtains, fridge, microwave and tea and coffee facilities. The grounds include a saltwater outdoor pool, barbecue facilities, gardens and outdoor seating. Wagga Airport and the RAAF base are about seven minutes away, and Lake Albert and the Botanic Gardens about eight.
highlights: Fridge and microwave in every room
About seven minutes to Wagga Airport and the RAAF base

name: BIG4 Ingenia Holidays Wagga Wagga
description: A riverside holiday park on Hammond Avenue about 2km from the Wagga Wagga town centre, backing onto the Murrumbidgee River. Accommodation covers cabins for different group sizes and budgets plus caravan and camping sites. Facilities include a swimming pool, adventure playground, camp kitchen, walking tracks, river access with a private boat launch, EV charging and a 24 hour service station. Some sites and cabins are pet friendly.
highlights: Cabins plus caravan and camping sites
Murrumbidgee River access and private boat launch

name: Horseshoe Tourist Park
description: A caravan park in a lagoon setting about seven minutes north of the Wagga Wagga CBD. Sites include drive-thru powered sites, ensuite powered sites and big rig sites, with two-bedroom standard cabins, deluxe studios and deluxe villas for cabin stays. Facilities cover an outdoor swimming pool, free barbecues, free Wi-Fi and a function room with an outdoor barbecue area. All sites are gravel and not suited to tents, swags or soft floor campers, and pets are not permitted. Charles Sturt University is about four minutes away.
highlights: Drive-thru, ensuite and big rig powered sites
Standard cabins, deluxe studios and deluxe villas
Function room with outdoor barbecue area
Four minutes from Charles Sturt University

name: Globe Apartments
description: Refurbished self-contained serviced apartments on the corner of Peter and Morgan Streets, one block from the main street. The building was the Globe Hotel in the 1880s. Apartments sleep up to six people, and the property has barbecue facilities and secure parking and takes both short and extended stays.
highlights: Self-contained apartments sleeping up to six
Housed in the 1880s Globe Hotel building

name: The Riverine Club
description: Wagga's private club, offering 13 guest rooms on the first floor for members, reciprocal members and their guests. Some rooms have balconies looking over the Murrumbidgee River. There are two large shared bathrooms, a sitting room and a breakfast area, with continental breakfast available on request and discounted rates for large groups and extended stays. Guests also get access to member facilities including the private members bar and billiards room.
highlights: 13 guest rooms in the Wagga CBD
Members bar, billiards room and squash court
Discounts for groups and extended stays

name: Brae View Villas 1 and 2
description: Two self-contained two-bedroom villas in a quiet residential part of Kooringal, each sleeping five. Both have fully equipped kitchens, large dining areas, lounges with televisions, central heating and cooling and lock-up garages. Lake Albert and its walking and cycling tracks are close by, as is the Kooringal Shopping Centre.
highlights: Fully equipped kitchens and lock-up garages
Near Lake Albert and Kooringal Shopping Centre

name: Rosewood Cottage
description: A holiday cottage in the leafy residential suburb of Turvey Park. It is a double brick post-war classic built by a local family in the forties, kept with its period detail and fitted out with restored vintage furnishings. It suits families and guests after a quiet location and retro character.
highlights: Double brick post-war cottage from the 1940s
Period detail and restored vintage furnishings

name: The Old Billiard Shop
description: A renovated corner shop in Turvey Park that was once a billiard store, now let as accommodation. The stay is one large room with brass sash windows and original floorboards, with blackout blinds on the oversized windows for privacy. The bathroom is reached through an enclosed outdoor area a few steps from the room, and all fixtures are newly installed.
highlights: Brass sash windows and original floorboards
Blackout blinds on the oversized windows
Bathroom via an enclosed outdoor area

name: Nice on Nilma
description: A self-contained Wagga Wagga cottage let through Henderson's Houses and aimed at groups who want their own beds rather than shared sleeping. It has seven separate beds, one double and six singles, across three bedrooms, plus a fully enclosed sun room. Split system air conditioning runs in the lounge and bedrooms.
highlights: Seven separate beds across three bedrooms
Suited to families and larger groups

name: The Leagues
description: A modern heritage-style three-storey home on Gurwood Street purpose built for overnight and short-term stays. Rooms take one to four people each and all have heating and cooling, with continental breakfast included. It is close to the Wagga Wagga CBD, the hospital, the RSL and the Murrumbidgee Turf Club, and within driving distance of Kapooka Army Base and the Forest Hill RAAF base.
highlights: Rooms for one to four people
Heating and cooling in all rooms
Near the CBD, hospital and Turf Club

name: Junee Tourist Park
description: A caravan and camping park within walking distance of the Junee Licorice and Chocolate Factory. It has two-bedroom self-contained cabins in budget and deluxe versions, plus powered, non-powered, tent and fifth wheeler sites and drive-through sites for caravans and motorhomes. Facilities include a camp kitchen, laundry and modern amenities. The park is pet friendly, has a dog agility park alongside it and looks out over Park Dam.
highlights: Budget and deluxe two-bedroom self-contained cabins
Large powered, non-powered and drive-through sites
Pet friendly with a dog agility park alongside
Walking distance to the Licorice and Chocolate Factory

name: The Crossing Motel
description: A Junee motel on Seignior Street with air conditioned rooms, free Wi-Fi and smart TVs. The Roundhouse Restaurant serves seasonal a la carte meals using locally sourced produce and puts together luncheon hampers, with the restaurant and bar running 7am to 9pm. There is a guests-only saltwater outdoor pool, free guest laundry and on-site parking with room for large vehicles, coach groups, car clubs and motorcycle groups.
